video.title: Video editing | Multina User Manual
video.body:
Go to explanation
MultinaUser Manual
Featured featuresWorkflow tipsExplanation listInstallationTerms of use
Home›Video

Video editing

Turn footage, text, and audio
into a video that is yours

Cut, layer, and add sound!

Read explanation

Choose a feature that interests you

27 items
Top · Project settings01Make your first video!OpenClose

Choose a size, arrange your assets, and export the finished video.

  1. Import media in an empty tab and drag it onto the desired track. Importing the first video may change the project size and fps to match the asset.
  2. Open “Width × Height / fps” at the top and check the output size and fps for landscape or portrait video. See also Choosing framing, size, and FPS.
  3. Press Space to play and adjust text, background music, and display durations. Save, then use “Export” to create the finished MP4.
※ Tip

Export includes the entire timeline. Use a separate project for a short test.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Video export in this version covers the entire timeline. Exporting only selected clips or a selected range is not supported. Use a separate tab for a short test project; do not shorten the original by deleting its clips.

Link to this explanation
Left · Media02Import your assetsOpenClose

Importing stores media in the list. Placing it on the timeline is a separate next step.

  1. Add media with “＋ Import media” or by dropping it into the media area. Storing it in the list and placing it on the timeline are separate actions.
  2. Drag videos and images to a video track, and audio to an audio track. Check that names, durations, and other information appear correctly.
  3. Click an asset with audio in the list to audition it; click again to stop. Clicking a still image is not audio auditioning.
  4. Heavy videos are optimized for preview on first use. “Lightweight” indicates a display copy; export uses the original asset.
  5. Right-click unwanted media and choose “Delete including managed copy”. If it is in use, also check how many clips will be deleted.
! Caution

“Delete including managed copy” also deletes clips that use the asset.

TypeSupported import extensions
Videomp4 / mov / avi / mkv / webm / flv / wmv / m4v / hevc / ts
Audiomp3 / wav / aac / flac / ogg / m4a / wma / aiff / aif / opus
Imagejpg / jpeg / png / webp / bmp / gif / tif / tiff
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The managed copy, thumbnail, and proxy are moved to the Recycle Bin. This differs from directly editing or deleting the original imported file.

A listed extension does not guarantee that a file can be read: its internal video/audio format or corruption may prevent loading. Do not treat media with a loading error as successfully imported.

Link to this explanation
Bottom · Timeline03Arrange, cut, and change durationsOpenClose

Move clips and drag their edges to adjust the portion used.

  1. Drag a clip’s body to move it in time or between tracks. Drag either edge to adjust the portion used.
  2. Move the playhead to the cut position and press F, or right-click and choose “Cut here”. You can then adjust the two resulting parts independently.
  3. Ctrl＋click adds to the selection. Before inserting copied clips, check the destination track and playhead position.
  4. Press R／Delete／Backspace to delete the selection. Right-click empty space to choose how to close gaps on this track or all tracks.
  5. After moving clips, play through joins and check synchronization with subtitles and background music. Reverse unintended changes with “Undo”.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

An action may be unavailable because of overlaps on the same track, insufficient space at the destination, or a locked linked track. Check tracks and neighboring clips instead of repeatedly trying the action.

Video and audio clip edges cannot be extended beyond the media's actual duration. This differs from adjusting the display duration of still images or text.

Delete on the timeline removes placed clips. “Delete including managed copy” in the media list also targets clips using that media, so read the count in the confirmation dialog.

Link to this explanation
Bottom · Timeline04Where you right-click matters!OpenClose

Clips, track names, empty space, and keyframe records each open different actions.

  1. Right-click a clip for asset actions, a track name for visibility, mute, lock, volume, order, and related controls, or empty space to add content or close gaps.
  2. Reorder tracks by dragging their names or using the right-click move commands. Track order also affects how video layers overlap.
  3. “Select line” and “Select from playhead onward” select multiple clips. Check the selection count and targets before acting.
  4. When closing gaps across all tracks, check which subtitles and audio will move together. Also check for locked tracks first.
※ Tip

When preserving synchronization across all tracks, check which audio and subtitle items will move too.

Right-click targetMain items
Video/image clipEffects, transitions, speed, volume, audio effects, Cut Here, and Delete. Videos containing audio also offer separation of video and audio.
Audio clipVolume, effects, speed, Cut Here, and Delete.
Track nameTrack volume, mute, lock, add a track above/below, move up/down, and delete track.
Empty timeline spaceClose the gap on this track only / close the same amount on all tracks. Layer tracks also offer items for adding content.
Multiple-selection menu0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2× speed and delete selected clips.
Recorded keyframesRecord the current state. Right-click a record button to delete that record.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Deleting a track also affects the items placed on it. Locking prevents editing; it does not hide the track.

B / N line selection may include multiple tracks. Check the selection count before deleting or changing speed in bulk.

Link to this explanation
Center · Preview05Viewing zoom versus asset sizeOpenClose

Preview zoom affects only the view. Adjust assets within the project using “Transform · Mask”.

  1. J／K and preview zoom change only the viewing size. At 110% or higher, use M＋left-drag to pan the view.
  2. For an asset within the project, use the selected clip’s “Transform · Mask” to change Position X／Y, Scale X／Y, Rotation, and Opacity.
  3. Choose “Cutout mask” → “Circle (wipe)” to make an inset. With the circle’s manipulation frame ON, adjust the circle’s position and size.
  4. Turn the manipulation frame OFF to move only the footage inside the circle. To remove the cutout itself, set the mask back to “None”.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

“Fit video to screen” resets the media's position and size. Do not confuse it with “All”, which resets preview zoom.

Reset Transform also affects transform settings such as the circular mask. If it resets settings you needed, use Undo.

Auto (Lightweight) / Original Size (Inspect Details) controls preview processing resolution. It does not change the output resolution or fps.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings06Add subtitles and titlesOpenClose

Text is a separate clip. Change its content, typeface, decoration, and display duration independently.

  1. Right-click empty space on a layer track → “Add text”, or press T to place it. Separate clips make subtitles and supplementary notes easier to adjust.
  2. On the right, use “Text” for content, font, bold, vertical writing, and alignment, and “Decoration” for outlines, shadows, glow, gradients, and more.
  3. Set position and size in the preview, then set display start and end on the timeline. Check legibility with the text over its background.
  4. Time lyrics to the actual singing. Set text entrance effects in “Motion” and review a short section repeatedly.
※ Tip

Time lyrics to when the singing actually starts, not to scene changes.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Cancel placement of media held with T or a media shortcut using Esc or right-click. You cannot add it at an invalid location or onto a locked track.

Small text and excessive decoration may be hard to read in a reduced-size finished video. Check at the actual viewing size too.

Text in a rasterized logo differs from normal text: you cannot retype its words in a text field.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings07Give text more ways to appearOpenClose

In “Motion” on the right, choose text entrances, color sweeps, and per-character movement.

  1. Select the text, then choose its entrance or movement in “Motion” on the right. Use per-character and whole-text motion for different purposes.
  2. Adjust period, amount, looping, and IN／OUT to suit the clip length. Check that strong effects do not make the text unreadable.
  3. For lyric wipes or karaoke color sweeps, set the start time, duration in seconds, sweep color, and boundary. These do not analyze audio automatically.
※ Tip

Wipes and color sweeps use specified durations in seconds. They do not synchronize automatically from audio.

TypeMotion
Vertical floatThe whole text floats up and down.
ShakeShakes the whole text.
Enter from Bottom / Enter from LeftThe whole text enters from below or from the left.
Jelly bounceThe whole text changes size with a bouncy motion.
Lyrics wipeReveals characters in order from the left.
Karaoke color sweepSweeps color from the left while keeping the text visible.
Per character · BubbleEach character expands with a time offset.
Per character · SwayCharacters sway left and right at different times.
Per character · WaveAn up-and-down wave travels from the first character onward.
NoneRemoves the motion type. Check fade settings separately.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Lyric Wipe and Karaoke Color Sweep advance according to duration. They do not analyze audio to synchronize lyrics automatically.

Karaoke Color Sweep and the 3 per-character types are for regular text and cannot be selected for text with a shape.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings08Animate with keyframesOpenClose

Record position, size, and other states at different times; the app connects them to create motion.

  1. Place the playhead inside the target clip and press L to turn keyframe editing ON. If an out-of-range message appears, first return the playhead to the clip.
  2. Set the first position, size, and other values, then move to another frame and set the next state. To record without changing the state, right-click and choose “Record current state”.
  3. Click a “○f” record to jump to that time. To delete it, right-click its record button and choose “Delete this record”.
  4. Play to check the motion, then turn L OFF when finished editing. Turning it OFF does not delete the recorded motion.
※ Tip

Recorded motion remains when keyframe editing is OFF.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If “Outside selected block range” appears, move the playhead back inside the target clip.

Mosaic / Blur uses outline records, not the same settings as normal position animation. A mosaic must retain at least 1 outline record.

This does not automatically analyze audio for positions or lyric timing. Check and adjust the specified frames or durations.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings09Faster, slower, or fitted to a durationOpenClose

Right-click video or audio → “Change speed”. Specify 0.1–8× speed or a desired duration.

  1. Right-click video or audio → “Change speed”. Set a speed of 0.1–8× or specify the duration you want.
  2. Turn “Preserve original pitch” ON to keep voices or music at their original pitch. Let pitch follow speed for a fast-forward-style sound.
  3. For slow-motion frame interpolation, choose sampling, blending, or optical flow. Compare the methods with short exports.
  4. Because the duration changes, also check linked items and overlaps with adjacent clips. If the change is rejected, first resolve conditions such as locked tracks.
Interpolation methodUses and cautions
Frame sampling (fast)The basic method selects the required frames. Start with this setting to establish duration.
Frame blendingBlends neighboring frames. Motion may look softer, but doubled outlines can appear.
Optical flow (high quality · slow)Estimates motion to generate intermediate frames. Processing is demanding, and rapid motion or occlusion may cause distortion, so check the exported result.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Changes may be blocked by overlaps with neighboring clips or a locked linked track. Check available space and linked tracks.

Frame Blend / Optical Flow are export-processing settings. Do not judge the final interpolation result from normal preview playback alone.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings10Choose color adjustments, decoration, and transitionsOpenClose

Right-click footage → “Effects”. Choose color presets, individual adjustments, decoration, or transitions.

  1. Right-click a video clip → “Effects” to open the settings on the right. Use “Filter” for color presets and “Custom” for individual values.
  2. Use “Style” for light or frames and “Switch” for joins between clips. Similar names may refer to effects applied in different places.
  3. Set filter strength first, then select a name to apply it. This replaces the previous video-effect group, so take care with adjustments you want to keep.
  4. After disabling or resetting effects, separate settings such as transitions or text motion may remain. Compare the settings panel with actual playback.
※ Tip

Choosing another filter replaces the previous video-effect group.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Choosing a filter replaces the target clip's combination of video effects. To retain earlier individual adjustments or decorations, check the result after applying it and use Undo if needed.

Reset Effects resets video effects. It does not also remove all separate settings such as transitions, text motion, audio, or transforms.

Check strong light, flashing, and abrupt color changes during continuous playback. The Fade effect name differs from fades at the start or end of a clip.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings11Set the color look with a filterOpenClose

Set the strength before choosing a preset name. Use “Custom” for fine adjustments afterward.

  1. In “Filter”, set the strength and then click the desired preset. Use the table below to choose the kind of color look.
  2. Moving the strength control alone does not rewrite an already applied combination. If needed, change the strength and select the preset again.
  3. For finer adjustments after applying a filter, open “Custom”. Use “Undo” or reset to compare with the previous appearance.
FilterUses and combined adjustments
CinemaCombines increased contrast, reduced saturation, and darker edges. Use it as a starting point for a defined cinematic look.
VintageSlightly raises brightness, reduces saturation, and adds warmth and shaded edges for an old-photo look.
CoolUses cooler color temperature and saturation for a cool impression.
WarmUses warmer color temperature and brightness for a warm impression.
BrighterRaises brightness. Check for clipped highlights.
DarkerLowers brightness. Check for crushed shadows.
More vividRaises saturation. Watch skin tones and oversaturated reds.
Black and whiteRemoves color to create grayscale.
DramaCombines stronger contrast, restrained saturation, and shaded edges.
FadeA pale look that raises brightness and reduces contrast and saturation.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Choosing another filter replaces the previous video effects. Make fine adjustments afterward under Custom.

Fade is a washed-out color preset, not a fade-out that disappears over time.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings12Fine-tune brightness and colorOpenClose

In “Effects” → “Custom”, adjust only the settings you need.

  1. In “Effects” → “Custom”, start with small changes to brightness, contrast, and saturation.
  2. For color temperature, tinting, sharpening, and similar effects, check the enabled state as well as the values. Choose between solid-color tinting, preserving light and dark detail, two-color tinting, and other modes.
  3. Compare skin tones, shadows, and white areas for lost color detail or overemphasized edges. Use the relevant setting’s reset to restore it.
itemsHow to choose and use it
BrightnessOverall brightness. Excessive increases lose highlight detail, so adjust while watching faces or the sky.
ContrastChanges the difference between light and dark. Check both shadows and highlights.
SaturationColor intensity. Colors become weaker as the value approaches 0.
HueRotates all colors. Use it for recoloring or effects rather than natural color correction.
Color TemperatureShifts toward warmer or cooler colors.
BlurBlurs the entire clip. To hide only part of it, use a Mosaic / Blur layer.
SharpenEmphasizes outlines. Check that fine edges and noise do not become too pronounced.
Color overlayOverlays a selected color on the original video. Useful when you also want to retain its original colors.
Single color (preserve shading)Shifts toward a single color while preserving light and dark detail.
DuotoneAssigns different colors to shadows and highlights. Useful for logo-like or graphic color schemes.
GrayscaleRemoves color to show light and dark values.
VignetteDarkens the edges to draw attention toward the center. Check that text or people at the edges do not become too dark.
Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings13Decorate with glow, color shifts, and framesOpenClose

Effects in “Style” can be combined. Adjust their strength and frame width.

  1. Turn on the decorations you need in “Style” and start with low strength. When combining decorations, check them one at a time.
  2. Adjust frame thickness, and the haze width for faded frames. Check that important text or faces near the screen edges are not obscured.
  3. Compare with a short playback that includes the beginning and end. Turn individual effects OFF to remove them, or use the Style reset to reset the decoration group.
StyleUses and adjustments
Soft FocusSoftens the image. Check the readability of small text.
GlowAdds a glowing look to bright areas. Lower the strength and compare so white regions do not spread too far.
VignetteA decorative darkening around the edges.
Chromatic AberrationOffsets colored outlines. Use for retro or digital effects, and check for doubled text.
White Line Border / Black Line BorderAdds a solid-color outline around the edge. Adjust it with “Border thickness”.
Gold Gradient Border / Rainbow Gradient BorderAdds a gold-toned or rainbow gradient border around the edge.
Black Fade Border / White Fade BorderExtends black or white haze inward from the edge. Line thickness and haze width can be adjusted independently.
Link to this explanation
Bottom · Timeline14Make smooth connections between cutsOpenClose

Right-click “Transition” to specify the start/end side, type, and duration.

  1. For transitions between 2 video clips, place them on the same track with their adjoining edges touching.
  2. Adjust direction and boundary settings. You can also open settings from the yellow transition interval.
  3. To remove one, choose “None” or “Delete this transition”.
※ Tip

Video transitions do not automatically crossfade audio.

TypeAppearance and additional settings
Cross dissolve (two videos)Fades the previous image into the next for a natural scene change.
Push (two videos)The next image pushes the previous one out. Choose left → right, right → left, top → bottom, or bottom → top.
Wipe (to next video)A moving boundary reveals the next image. Adjust direction and boundary softness.
Iris (next video expands)The next image expands from a circular or square area. Choose the shape and boundary softness.
Slide (next video enters)The next image enters from the specified direction. Choose the direction.
Zoom (next video expands)The next image appears as it enlarges.
Glitch (irregular bands)Transitions using irregular disrupted bands. Adjust the strength.
Noise dissolve (static)Transitions through static-like noise. Adjust the strength.
White fadeUses white at the start or end of the clip.
White flashAdds a white flash. Adjust the strength and avoid repeated strong flashes at short intervals.
BlurUses blur at the start or end. Adjust the strength.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Transitions between adjoining videos composite them without a black gap. Edge frames are held outside the edited interval; this does not extend clip durations or audio positions to join them.

Link Adjacent Clips does not set an automatic audio crossfade. Adjust audio fades separately.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings15Make a background color transparentOpenClose

Remove a solid-color background to reveal the footage underneath.

  1. Right-click a video or image → open “Chroma key (transparent background)” and turn it ON.
  2. Specify the color to remove or sample the background from the unprocessed asset. Put the footage to reveal on a lower track.
  3. Start with a low tolerance and increase it while checking that hair or similarly colored clothing is not removed. Adjust edge smoothing and spill removal in small amounts too.
  4. Check moving edges during playback and in a short export. In ordinary video output, keyed areas with no asset underneath become black.
※ Tip

This is not automatic person cutout. Check that hair or clothing of the same color is not removed.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Positive Edge Adjustment values tighten the outline; negative values retain semitransparent areas. “Remove background residue” also makes faint areas mixed with the background color transparent, so take care with similarly colored clothing.

“Remove color spill” reduces background color remaining on outlines. It does not expand the transparent area itself.

Changes apply when you release the slider or pause for about 0.35 seconds. Transparent regions with no media underneath appear and export as black in normal video output. This is not a setting for exporting transparent video.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings16Hide only part of the pictureOpenClose

Add a region-based mosaic or blur to a layer track.

  1. Add a mosaic or blur to a layer track above the subject to hide. Match the effect clip’s start and end to the required interval.
  2. Place the playhead in that interval and turn L ON. Choose a circle, rectangle, or other shape, its outline, and mosaic size or blur strength.
  3. Record the outline at times when the subject moves. Do not confuse turning preview visibility ON/OFF with deleting the clip.
  4. This is not automatic tracking. Play the entire file intended for publication and check for exposure even at cuts and moments of movement.
! Caution

This is not automatic tracking. Check the entire finished video before publishing.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

This is not automatic tracking or face recognition. Add records manually to follow the subject's movement.

Preview Display OFF toggles the viewing aid. To remove the concealment effect itself from the finished video, check the target layer's settings, mute, or deletion.

When hiding personal information, inspect the entire finished file, not just the editing preview. A strength value alone does not guarantee adequate concealment.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings17Balance voices and background musicOpenClose

Adjust clip and track volume, fades, and audio effects.

  1. Select an audio clip and check clip volume, track volume, and gain. Raising them together too far causes distortion.
  2. To edit audio separately from the picture, right-click the video and choose “Separate video and audio”. The original video’s sound is stopped to avoid doubling.
  3. Audio settings on the right take effect immediately; a window opened by right-click takes effect with “Apply”. Adjust volume and fade durations in seconds.
  4. Compare with the original sound and listen for muffled voices, distortion, or unnatural noise reduction. These settings are separate from preset audition volume.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Separate Video and Audio does not rewrite the original file. Distinguish it from repeatedly extracting the same sound from a video that has already been separated.

If the picture is muted after separation, right-click the video and choose Show Separated Video Again to restore it. The original video's audio remains stopped.

When changing the speed or other properties of separated linked clips, the linked clip's state also matters. If a linked track lock or overlap with a neighboring clip blocks the change, resolve that condition first.

The audition volume for preset media does not change timeline or export volume.

Link to this explanation
Right · Effect settings18Audio effects at a glanceOpenClose

Choose the effects your voice or background music needs, and compare them with the original sound.

  1. Select the target audio, or right-click a video and open “Audio effects”. Choose a suitable setting from the table below.
  2. Use EQ and volume for voice clarity, fades for entrances and exits, and small amounts of reverb or similar effects for a sense of space.
  3. Wait for the first noise-reduction processing to finish. Turn it OFF to compare with the original and check that voices or music are not being removed too.
  4. Listen through to the end of a short export too. Effect tails stop at the clip’s end, so consider the clip length carefully.
※ Tip

Listen to reverb tails and noise-reduction results all the way to the end of the clip.

itemsWhat to choose and how to use it
Clip Volume / GainRaises or lowers the target clip's sound. Start by lowering background music relative to louder foreground sound.
PanAdjusts left/right positioning. Center is the reference position.
Speed0.1–8×. Audio duration also changes. Check for overlaps with neighboring clips.
PitchChanges pitch in semitones. If Link Speed and Pitch is ON, pitch changes caused by speed are added too.
Link Speed and Pitch / Preserve Original PitchChoose between a high-pitched sped-up voice and keeping the original pitch when changing speed.
Fade In / OutSpecify how many seconds volume changes over at the beginning and end. If both fade intervals overlap in a short clip, the whole clip becomes quieter.
Fade curveIn the right-click audio settings, choose Linear, Constant Power, or Exponential and compare the attack and decay. This does not automatically overlap adjacent audio clips.
Equalizer: Low / Mid / HighAdjust low frequencies, the central voice range, and high frequencies separately. Start by slightly reducing unwanted ranges and comparing.
CompressorTurn it ON and set the threshold, where compression begins, and the ratio. It reduces loud sounds to even out volume differences.
ReverbTurn it ON and use amount/mix and decay time to add room ambience. Start with a small amount so voices do not sound too distant.
DelayTurn it ON and adjust repeat interval, feedback strength, and amount/mix. It creates echo-like repetitions.
Low cut (low-frequency noise)Turn it ON and specify a frequency to reduce low-frequency content. Use for low rumble and muddiness; it differs from hiss removal.
Noise reduction (hiss · steady noise)Turn it ON and adjust reduction amount and noise floor. It targets steady noise such as air conditioning. Excessive settings also damage voices and music, so compare with OFF.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The settings window opened by right-click requires Apply. The inspector on the right applies changes immediately.

Reverb and delay tails do not continue indefinitely beyond the clip's end. Always audition how the sound ends.

Audio playback of the target clip waits until initial noise-reduction processing finishes. If processing fails, turn it OFF and check the original audio.

Link to this explanation
Bottom · Timeline19Freeze a video with a screenshot!OpenClose

A full screenshot includes text and effects. After inserting it, the still image can return to the original continuation.

  1. Place the playhead at the desired time and choose a screenshot of only the target cut or the entire composition. The full version also composites text, mosaics, and other elements.
  2. Inserting the full screenshot into the timeline splits the visual blocks at that time and moves their later portions after a 2-second still image. When the still ends, playback resumes from the same continuation.
  3. Audio belonging to the original video and linked audio also pause during that interval. Independent background music and unlinked audio continue playing.
  4. Check the video track used for insertion and synchronization before and after it. Managed and downloadable image copies are saved separately.
※ Tip

Managed and downloadable image copies are saved separately.

TargetBehavior during full-screenshot insertion
Video, text, and overlaid imagesResume from the original continuation after a 2-second still
Embedded video audio / audio linked to videoPause during the still, then resume with the picture
Independent / unlinked audioContinue without moving
Image fileSaved as a managed copy and a separate copy in Downloads
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If full-screenshot insertion would break a transition, a message prevents insertion. You can still save the image. If a target track is locked, unlock it or use save only.

The dedicated managed copy and the downloaded copy are separate. Organizing the download does not directly delete the project's copy.

Link to this explanation
Left · Media20Recall your favorite assetsOpenClose

G opens presets; H opens custom sets. Reuse backgrounds, text, sound effects, and more.

  1. Press G for presets or H for custom sets, then drag an asset card to a compatible track.
  2. Use “＋ Save custom preset” for assets you use repeatedly. A clip’s right-click “Save custom preset (keep settings)” also lets you reuse its editing settings.
  3. Right-click a supported card to assign a key. Tap the key then click, or hold it while choosing a position and release to place the asset.
  4. “Shortcut settings” separates standard actions from added assets. Deleting a registration is different from deleting clips already placed in a project.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Four BGMer tracks are included: Electric Town Devil (BPM 108), Colorful Street (BPM 120), The Landscape of That Day (BPM 180), and Crystals of Tears (BPM 81). Preview a track, then drag it to an audio track. Right-click each card to assign its own shortcut.

Custom categories include Background Music, Sound Effects, Fonts, Text, Images, Videos, and Mosaic / Blur. Available registration categories depend on the media type.

If an entry with the same name exists, read the replacement target and confirmation. Also read the confirmation before deleting registered media.

Check the media's license terms before using fonts or redistributing assets.

Link to this explanation
Top · Project settings21Take an editable project with youOpenClose

Editable Video data is a .veproject folder. Keep the entire folder, including its assets.

  1. Save your edits and choose a destination with project “Export”. The .veproject folder containing project.json and assets is the editable project data.
  2. Keep and move the whole folder. Extracting just project.json or the footage may prevent assets from loading again.
  3. Use “Import” to select the .veproject folder. Read the confirmation about loading into the current tab, then check assets and the editing state.
※ Tip

An MP4 cannot restore the original subtitles or clip structure.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

This does not reconstruct original subtitles, clips, or effect settings from a finished MP4. Keep the .veproject too for work you may revise later.

Check media and additional-font license terms separately. Being able to export them does not mean you may redistribute them to others.

Link to this explanation
Top · Project settings22Export your finished video!OpenClose

Creates an MP4 of the entire timeline. Size and fps come from the project settings.

  1. Save the project and play it through to the end. Check for forgotten clips far down the timeline, unwanted gaps, and subtitles left on screen.
  2. Set size and fps in the project’s “Width × Height / fps”. Check the values displayed on the output screen.
  3. In “Export”, choose the encoder and quality. Start by trying automatic H.264 with video bitrate 0 (automatic).
  4. Choose a save location and start output as .mp4. After completion, use “Open save location” to check the picture, sound, and duration. Use the dedicated button to cancel.
! Caution

Finishing work may still be in progress near 99%. Do not force quit before completion.

SettingsHow to choose / scope in this version
H.264 AutoTests supported NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs in actual operation and uses the CPU if none works. If GPU compression fails partway through, it also retries on the CPU using intermediate data.
H.264 NVIDIA NVENC / Intel Quick Sync / AMD AMFSpecifies the GPU encoding method. Check your PC's support; if it fails, try H.264 Auto or CPU.
HEVC AMD／AV1 AMDCompression methods for supported GPUs. Use a short export to verify that the intended player supports MP4 containing HEVC or AV1.
H.264 CPU／HEVC CPUCompresses on the CPU. Processing may take longer.
High Quality / Balanced / Speed PriorityA choice between quality and compression time. High Quality is not lossless storage either.
Target / Maximum Video BitrateUnits are kbps. 0 selects an automatic value based on the project's resolution and fps. Do not confuse this with Mbps in recording settings.
Audio bitrate192 / 256 / 320 kbps. The default is 256 kbps.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

There is no range setting for exporting only a selection or selected clips. Prepare a separate short test project for test exports.

Even if MKV and MOV appear in the save dialog, the current Video workspace passes MP4 as the output container. Save as .mp4 instead of merely changing the extension.

Final saving may continue around 99% progress. Check for the Completed message and a playable finished file. Do not treat files left by errors or cancellation as finished outputs.

GPU use mainly speeds up final compression. Not every stage, including compositing and text processing, runs solely on the GPU.

Link to this explanation
Top · Project settings23Video keys and troubleshootingOpenClose

Check current assignments in “Shortcut settings”. The table below shows the defaults.

  1. Add, change, or clear keys in the settings list. You can also change them by right-clicking supported buttons.
  2. Register asset-card keys by right-clicking too. Standard actions and added assets are shown separately in settings.
KeyDefault action
SpacePlay/Stop
F / TCut / add text (specify placement for T)
C / VCopy / paste (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V also supported)
R / Delete / BackspaceDelete
Z / XUndo / redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z also supported)
A / D or ← / →Back / forward 1 frame; hold to accelerate
Q / EBack / forward 10 seconds; hold for 60 seconds
W / S or ↑ / ↓Select the track above / below (does not reorder tracks)
J / KZoom the preview in / out
M + left-dragPan the zoomed preview
Y / UGo to the start / end of the selection or selected clip
I / OGo to the start / end of the project
BSelect clips extending beyond the playhead
NSelect clips intersecting the playhead
G / HOpen Presets / Custom Sets
LToggle keyframe editing ON / OFF
− / ＋Zoom the timeline out / in (numeric keypad − / + also supported)
Ctrl+SSave project
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Tap A / D for 1 frame, or hold to accelerate. Tap Q / E for 10 seconds, or hold to move in 60-second increments.

Right-click supported buttons with key labels to edit their assignments. Settings list standard actions separately from media shortcuts registered later.

If playback is slow, try Auto (Lightweight) video preview. Preview zoom and lightweight display do not change project resolution or export quality.

Link to this explanation
Top · Project settings24Choose landscape or portrait framing and FPSOpenClose

Width and height determine the finished video’s framing; fps is the number of frames per second. Enter dimensions for landscape, portrait, or square output.

  1. Click “Width × Height / fps” at the top. Enter dimensions for your purpose, such as 1920 × 1080 for landscape, 1080 × 1920 for portrait, or 1080 × 1080 for square.
  2. 4K, 2K, FHD, HD, and SD are shortcuts to landscape sizes. For portrait video, enter the width and height in the opposite order yourself.
  3. Enter a value such as 30 or 60 in the fps field and confirm with OK. Size and fps also apply to the exported MP4; they are separate from preview zoom.
  4. Changing the frame dimensions alone does not automatically recompose assets. Check each clip’s position and scale, and whether text or frames are cut off.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Importing the first video may change the project size and fps to match the original asset. Check the intended values after importing.

Raising fps alone does not add motion absent from the original asset. Decide by comparing performance, file size, and a short output.

Link to this explanation
Center · Preview25Choose lightweight or original-size previewOpenClose

Reducing the display load is separate from finished-video quality. Switch to original size when you need to inspect details.

  1. For a heavy video’s first use, wait for preview optimization. This creates a display cache without changing the original video.
  2. Under “Preview”, choose automatic (lightweight) or original size (detail inspection). Original size increases display load; return to lightweight after checking edges or text.
  3. Changing display zoom is another separate action. Preview-quality selection does not change output resolution, fps, or source assets.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If optimization fails, read the message about displaying the original. An unavailable lightweight preview alone does not mean the asset or export is broken.

Link to this explanation
Bottom · Timeline26Switch GIF looping on or offOpenClose

After placing a GIF on a video track, right-click the clip to turn looping ON／OFF.

  1. Import a .gif into Media and drag it onto a video track. Timeline actions are unavailable while it is only in the media list.
  2. Right-click the GIF clip on the timeline → “GIF loop: ON／OFF (toggle)”. This option appears only for GIF assets.
  3. Adjust the clip’s display duration and play it. Check that ON repeats the animation and OFF does not.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

GIF loop settings are separate from text-motion looping.

Link to this explanation
Top · Project settings27Restore a video from save historyOpenClose

Use current-edit saving and dated save history for different purposes. History also lets you continue along a different path from an earlier state.

  1. At important milestones, press “Save” at the top. Manual-save history is available in Project list.
  2. In “Project list” → “Restore (dated save history)”, choose the project and one of the latest 3 save times.
  3. Check the current destination tab before restoring. Assets are also copied independently, so the restoration source is not changed directly.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The latest 3 history entries are not unlimited backups. For long-term storage, export a .veproject to another location.

Link to this explanation
Multina28A facecam for gameplay commentary

Place the presenter above the gameplay, then crop the presenter into a circular inset.

  1. Put gameplay on a lower video track and the presenter on a higher video track.
  2. Select the presenter clip → Transform / Mask → Cutout mask → Circle (wipe).
  3. Turn the circle-frame control ON to move or resize the circle. Turn it OFF to reposition the presenter inside the unchanged circle.
  4. Balance gameplay, music and microphone volume. A visual mask does not mute audio.
Workflow tips29Your favorite assets, one key awayOpenClose

Save a favorite sound as a custom preset and recall it with your own key. This video-editing example covers saving, assigning and placing it.

1. Save the asset as a custom preset

Choose a file with “Save custom preset”, check its name and category, then select “Register”. This example saves the sound “Demo Impact”.

2. Right-click the saved card to assign a key

Open “Custom set” and right-click the saved asset card. Select the key field, press your chosen key, then select “Confirm”. The example uses F6.

3. Recall with the key and place on the timeline

Finish text entry, then tap the key to pick up the asset. For a sound, click the desired position on an audio track to place it.

※ Tip

F6 is assigned for this example, not a default. Choose an unused key or a Ctrl/Shift combination. Review, change or remove it in Shortcut settings → Added shortcuts.

You can also hold the key, move the pointer to the destination and release to place. Right-click to cancel. Use an unlocked, compatible track: audio for sounds, video for images and footage. Simply clicking an asset card does not add it.

Reuse a finished clip, too

Right-click a timeline clip to save it as a custom preset, including its text, decoration, placement, audio and effect settings. Useful for recurring headlines and sound presets.

※ Notes

Image editing also supports custom assets and recall keys. In Comics · Illustration, save a custom pen and assign its Recall key in pen settings. Shortcuts are independent in each tool.

Custom assets in ImageCustom pens in Comics · Illustration

image.body:

MultinaUser Manual
Featured featuresWorkflow tipsExplanation listInstallationTerms of use
Home›Image

Image editing

Photos and text,
just as you imagine

Create freely with layers!

Read explanation

Choose a feature that interests you

21 items
Top · Tools01Make your first image!OpenClose

Keep backgrounds, people, and text on separate layers for detailed adjustments later.

  1. Open an empty tab. For fixed dimensions, use “Canvas settings” at the upper left to specify width, height, and transparency or background color.
  2. Import an image into Media; click it to place it in the center or drag it to a chosen position. Importing alone does not place it on the canvas.
  3. Put people, backgrounds, and headings on separate layers. Enter content with “Text”, then adjust decoration and positioning on the right.
  4. Check layer stacking, wait for saving to finish, and use “Export”. Also export editable project data if you want to revise it later.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

An empty tab starts at 1280×720px. If “Automatically match the size of the first image placed.” is shown, clicking an image in the media list to place it resizes the canvas to that image's dimensions. This differs from dragging it to a specific position.

After you resize the canvas manually, images no longer resize it automatically. Supported canvases have a maximum side length of 8192px and a total of 32 million pixels.

Canvas Settings changes the finished image's bounds. It does not scale all photos and text already placed on it together.

Link to this explanation
Left · Assets02Importing and placing are separate actionsOpenClose

Images are copied into Media on the left. From there, place them as layers as many times as needed.

  1. Use “＋ Import image file” or drop files into the import area. For a copied image, you can also use “Add from clipboard”.
  2. Click an image in the list to place it in the center, or drag it to a chosen position. Each placement adds an image layer.
  3. Search assets by name and other information. To organize them, right-click “Remove from media” and check the effect on assets currently in use.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Removing media retains managed files needed by placed layers or save history. Unused managed copies move to the Recycle Bin; this does not delete the original imported file.

“Image save folder” opens the managed storage location. To transfer editable work, use project data export instead of moving managed files by hand.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas03Edit at a comfortable viewing sizeOpenClose

Zooming or panning the view does not change project dimensions or asset positions.

  1. Zoom with “Fit to screen”, 100%, or Ctrl＋wheel.
  2. Pan with the hand tool, middle-button drag, or WASD.
  3. Use focused view for more space, and return with J or the exit button.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

With Hand active, dragging media pans the view instead of moving the media. Click Hand again to return to normal media manipulation.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings04Check stacking, visibility, and locksOpenClose

Higher layers appear in front. Drag to reorder, and use locks to protect edits.

  1. Select a card or an asset on the canvas. Shift＋click adds to or removes from the selection; some settings can adjust multiple items together.
  2. Higher layers appear in front. Drag to reorder and check the insertion position before releasing. You can scroll the list with the wheel while dragging.
  3. Check visibility, lock, opacity, and fx states. Hiding does not delete the asset; locking prevents movement and setting changes.
  4. Rename with right-click “Rename”. The same menu also offers duplicate, delete, and move to front/back.
※ Tip

Turning fx OFF also temporarily disables chroma key and text decorations.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Hiding is not deletion. Hidden layers remain in editable project data but do not appear in the finished image.

Locked layers cannot be moved or have their settings changed. If an item will not move, check its lock in the list on the right.

Turning fx OFF temporarily disables not only color and outline effects but also chroma key, text outlines, glow, and more. If a background reappears, check fx too.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas05Move, transform, and cropOpenClose

Adjust using the asset frame or “Positioning” on the right. Cropping hides part of the asset.

  1. Select the target and specify X／Y, width, height, and rotation in “Positioning” on the right. Corner handles scale, side squares adjust width or height, and the top circle rotates.
  2. Check “Lock aspect ratio”. Shift temporarily releases it; holding Shift during rotation snaps to 15° increments.
  3. Turn right-click “Edit crop” ON and adjust the frame around the area to keep. Turn crop editing OFF when finished.
  4. Turning “Apply crop” OFF lets you compare with the uncropped version; it is different from leaving edit mode. “Reset” removes the crop area itself.
※ Tip

The crop remains applied when crop editing is OFF.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Cropping is not available for Mosaic / Blur area layers. Select a supported layer such as an image, text, or shape.

Changing canvas zoom does not change layer dimensions or output image dimensions. To make viewing easier, use 100%, “Fit to screen”, or Ctrl + wheel.

Cropping does not erase captured information from the original file. Sharing project data containing the original image differs from sharing the finished image.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools06Draw with the marker and erase with the eraserOpenClose

Added drawing goes on a marker layer. The eraser affects only one selected layer.

  1. Choose “Marker”, set a round or chisel tip, color, thickness, and opacity, then draw. Drawing goes on a marker layer rather than being baked directly into the photo.
  2. If an editable marker layer is selected, drawing continues there. Otherwise, a new marker layer is created.
  3. Select one layer to erase and check that it is visible and unlocked. You can partially erase images, text, and shapes too.
  4. Undo mistakes with Z. To finish using a tool and return to normal interaction, press the selected tool button again.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Eraser does not erase all layers at once and does not work on Mosaic / Blur area layers. If nothing erases, check the target, visibility, and lock.

If a drawing-limit message appears, continue on a new marker layer. The original image file is not changed.

These Image tools are separate from the pen and pressure settings in Comics & Illustration.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings07Make text the starOpenClose

Add typefaces, outlines, shadows, and glow to text layers whose content remains editable.

  1. Add a layer with “Text”, then use “Decoration” on the right to adjust content, font, text size, color, bold, vertical writing, and alignment.
  2. “Positioning” controls the text layer’s location and frame size. Separate headings and supporting text to change their sizes and decorations independently.
  3. Edit text at the top of Transform, Style, or Adjust. These inputs update the same text layer, so content stays synchronized across tabs. Enable only the outlines, shadows, glow, and gradients you need.
  4. If text or large decorations are clipped, enlarge the positioning frame. Also check readability at the reduced size you will actually use.
※ Tip

Text in a rasterized logo cannot be rewritten in the text-content field.

DecorationAvailable adjustments
Double outlineSeparate colors and widths for outer and inner outlines. Helps distinguish the edges when text and background have similar colors.
ShadowShadow color, blur, Shadow X, and Shadow Y. Sets the direction and distance of the shadow's offset from the text.
GlowGlow color, width, and strength. Compare settings: even on a dark background, excessive glow can obscure letter shapes.
Text gradientStart color, end color, and angle. Toggle it separately from the solid text color.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Text is drawn inside its layer frame. If text or large decoration is clipped, enlarge the frame's width/height under “Positioning”. You do not have to reduce the font size instead.

Logo text baked into an image cannot be changed in the content field. Distinguish text layers from image layers.

For additional fonts and reusable text decoration, see Text presets, additional fonts, and textures.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings08Reuse text designsOpenClose

Presets apply an appearance. Added fonts and .mtext files also let you take decorations elsewhere.

  1. Apply a sample in “Text” → “Decoration” → “Preset”. It changes the appearance while preserving content, position, and size.
  2. Use “Adjust texture and trails” to set raised, metallic, or other textures and the number, spacing, direction, and color of trails. Trails are static decorations.
  3. Use “Added fonts” → “＋ Import file” to add TTF／OTF／WOFF／WOFF2, then choose a sample or an entry in the font list.
  4. Save the appearance with “Save current text decoration”. Use the sample’s “Export” to create a .mtext file for another environment.
※ Tip

.mtext does not save text content, position, or size. Use a saved layer to reuse the whole item unchanged.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

.mtext decoration settings do not store content, position, or size. To reuse a fixed heading's wording and placement too, use Saved Layers.

Registered fonts and text decorations are available in other image projects. Deleting an entry from the additional list leaves dedicated copies in projects already using it.

The ability to add or bundle fonts does not mean redistribution is permitted. Check the destination and license terms.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings09Decorate with shapes and card bordersOpenClose

Find basic shapes at the top, illustration assets in presets on the left, and overall frames in Card border on the right.

  1. Add a rectangle or circle and change fill, outline, and line width in “Decoration”. No fill makes the inside transparent; rectangles also support rounded corners.
  2. Drag arrows, hearts, enclosing frames, and similar assets from presets on the left. “Card border” on the right adds a frame fitted to the canvas.
  3. Select the added frame and use “Border settings” to adjust interior transparency, canvas following or free sizing, margins, and more.
  4. Manually moving or transforming a frame switches it to free sizing. Also arrange its layer order, for example in front of the background but behind the text.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The edge squares adjust height and width independently while preserving line width and corner rounding. Moving or transforming a canvas-fitted frame manually switches it to free size.

To place decoration in front of the background but behind text, change its order in Layers after adding it.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings10Color and perimeter effectsOpenClose

First choose “Selected layer” or “All” and verify the target.

  1. In “Effects” on the right, first choose Selected layer or All. Applying an effect only to a person differs from applying it to the entire composited image.
  2. Choose a color look and adjust its strength and palette. Even monochrome shadows and highlights can use colors other than black and white.
  3. In “Perimeter”, choose transparent fade, vignette, or aura, then adjust width, blur, opacity, and any available colors.
  4. “Adjustments” below contains brightness, contrast, saturation, and blur. Use the slider or adjacent numeric field and compare ON／OFF.
※ Tip

For light or borders following a person’s silhouette, use “Outline decoration”, not Perimeter.

TypeAppearance and use
Neon Duo / Amber / BlueColor effects using 2 colors. You can change the default palette.
Monochrome / Single colorCreates tonal gradation using shadow and highlight colors. You can choose 2 colors other than black and white.
Linear burnUses the specified color for a deeper, darker tone. Start with a small strength value.
Transparent fadeMakes the edges increasingly transparent. The result depends on the layers underneath and the canvas background.
VignetteTints the edges toward a specified color to draw attention to the center.
AuraMakes the image's outer edges appear to glow in a specified color.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

“Perimeter” processes the outside edges of the target image. To add a white outline or light following a transparent person's silhouette, use Contour decoration.

Use “Tone · Perimeter ON” to compare these settings and “Remove tone and perimeter effects” to remove them. Reset Adjustments is separate: it returns brightness, contrast, and saturation to 100% and blur to 0.

“Reset color and strength” differs from “Remove tone and perimeter effects”. Resetting values does not remove the selected effect.

For Mosaic / Blur area layers, adjust strength in their Mosaic or Blur settings on the right, not these color presets.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings11Make people and text stand outOpenClose

Add outlines, glow, and shadows around the nontransparent shape.

  1. Select a person or another asset, then open “Outline decoration” in Settings → “Decoration”. The same settings are available in the effects panel’s selected-layer area.
  2. Turn on only the outer glow, outline, and shadow you need. Start with small values for color-related effects, spread, blur, and opacity.
  3. Set shadow direction with horizontal and vertical offsets. Use light for soft separation from the background or an outline for a crisp boundary.
※ Tip

On a photo with a background, the effect follows the rectangular image’s outside edge. Remove the background first to follow a person’s silhouette.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

In a photo with an opaque background, the rectangular image boundary is used, not just the person. To follow a person's silhouette, use transparent media or a chroma-key result.

A text layer's own Double Outline, Shadow, and Glow are separate from “Outline decoration”. Combining them strengthens the effect, so toggle each individually to compare.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings12Transparency and blending colorsOpenClose

Opacity controls transparency. “Blend” changes how colors combine with layers below.

  1. Select the upper layer and open Settings → “Adjustments” → “Blend”. First check its original appearance in Normal mode.
  2. Try Multiply to combine darker components or Screen for light. Reduce layer opacity if the result is too strong.
  3. The same blend mode looks different against different backgrounds. Check over the actual background that text and people retain detail.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Blend Mode results depend on the colors below. An isolated layer over transparency may not make the effect easy to judge.

Linear Burn in the color-tone menu and Color Burn in the blend menu are different processes.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings13Make a solid-color background transparentOpenClose

This removes a specified color from an image. It does not automatically cut out complex backgrounds.

  1. Select the image and open Settings → “Background transparency”, or right-click “Chroma key (transparent background)”.
  2. Turn it ON and specify the background color, or click using “Pick color from image”. Press Esc to cancel color picking.
  3. Adjust tolerance, edge smoothing, and spill removal in small amounts. Zoom in to check that similarly colored hair or clothing is not removed.
  4. Inspect edges against checkerboard, white, black, or gray checking backgrounds. For transparent output, also make the canvas background transparent and choose PNG／WebP.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Reduce “Remove background residue” to retain large semitransparent areas such as smoke or veils. A stronger value is not always cleaner.

The inspection background is excluded from exports. However, an opaque canvas background color or background layer placed underneath is included in the finished image.

Reset Transparency Settings restores transparency values to their defaults. To disable transparency processing itself, uncheck Chroma Key (Transparent Background). The original image file is unchanged.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas14Process only an enclosed areaOpenClose

Enclosed mosaic or blur creates a dedicated layer that affects images underneath.

  1. Choose mosaic or blur, select freehand, rectangular, or circular enclosure, then drag. A new region layer is added.
  2. Adjust mosaic size or blur strength in the settings on the right. Move, rotate, or scale to correct the region.
  3. Put assets to process below the region layer and unprocessed text or other items above it. Compare using fx ON／OFF.
※ Tip

When hiding information, check that it is unreadable in the finished image too.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

When hiding personal information, zoom into the actual exported image and confirm it is unreadable. Weak blur or excessive transparency may not conceal enough.

Project data containing an area layer still retains the original image. Sharing a concealed finished image differs from sharing project data with its source media.

Link to this explanation
Left · Assets15Custom assets and saved layersOpenClose

Use Custom to reuse an image alone. Use Saved layers to preserve position and decoration too.

  1. Import and register images in Custom on the left. Registration alone does not place them; drag the card onto the canvas.
  2. Right-click “Saved layers” to register a finished layer arrangement. You can also open registration from a layer’s right-click menu and register multiple selected layers.
  3. A normal click on “Saved layers” opens the list. Clicking a card creates new layers with the registered position, size, and decoration.
  4. Right-click supported cards to assign recall keys. Assets do not scale automatically for different canvas dimensions; adjust placement after adding them.
What to reuseWhere to use it
Original image assetCustom on the left → ＋ Import and register image
Layer arrangement including position, size, and text contentSaved Layers at the top → Register Selected Layers
Text appearance without content or placementText on the right → Decoration → Added fonts → Save current text decoration
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Saved layers do not scale automatically when the current canvas differs from the canvas used at registration. Check the recorded dimensions and adjust under “Positioning” after adding them.

Custom assets and saved layers work in other image projects. Deleting the registered source leaves copies already placed in projects. Deleting a registration differs from deleting project layers.

You can edit a custom card's name field. Delete using × on a custom card or × in the saved-layer list, checking the target name first.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Settings16Right-click actions at a glanceOpenClose

Right-click an asset for that layer’s actions. Right-click empty space for a different menu.

  1. Right-clicking an asset targets that layer. Right-clicking empty space opens a menu with the selection cleared; actions requiring a target are unavailable.
  2. A layer copy remains editable, while “Copy entire canvas as image” produces one flattened image. Choose according to your purpose.
  3. Click “Saved layers” for the list; right-click to register. Right-click supported buttons with key hints to change shortcuts.
Right-click targetMain actions
Media on the canvas / Layers on the rightRename, edit/apply/reset crop, chroma key, copy, paste, duplicate, delete, bring to front/send to back, move one level, register saved layers, lock, and more. Some items are disabled depending on the target.
Images in Media on the leftRemove from media
Preset / Custom cards on the leftShortcut settings for that asset
Cards in the Saved Layers listShortcut settings for those saved layers
Saved Layers at the topRegister selected layers
Action buttons with key labelsShortcut settings for that action
Link to this explanation
Top · Tools17Protect your work with saving and historyOpenClose

In addition to autosaving while you work, the Save button records history at milestones.

  1. Use Save at the top or Ctrl＋S and check the saved status. If autosave fails, retry rather than assuming the save succeeded.
  2. To restore an earlier state, choose a date and time in Project list → “Save history (latest 3)” and restore it to the current workspace slot.
  3. “Clear layer” in Reset empties the current arrangement and can be reversed with “Undo”. It is not project deletion.
  4. Export a .multina-image for long-term storage or moving to another PC. Do not rely on only the latest 3 history entries as a long-term backup.
※ Tip

Save history is not an unlimited backup.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Project List contains states recorded by Save or before export. These are not necessarily the same point as autosave while working in a BOX. Each project retains the latest 3 save-history entries.

Reset does not delete media, original imported files, or other projects. Distinguish it from deleting the project itself.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools18Keep finished images and editable dataOpenClose

Finished-image export uses PNG／JPEG／WebP. Editable project transfer uses .multina-image.

  1. Save and inspect the canvas, then choose PNG／JPEG／WebP in finished-image “Export”. Change output dimensions through Canvas settings.
  2. JPEG／WebP also let you specify quality. JPEG cannot be transparent, so choose a background color. For PNG／WebP, make the canvas background transparent if needed.
  3. Use “Export” to choose a name and location. After completion, inspect the image in another viewer too.
  4. “Send PNG to video media” sends a flattened PNG to Video’s media list. It does not place it on the timeline automatically.
  5. For an editable backup, use project “Export” to create a .multina-image and “Import” to load it again. A finished PNG cannot restore the original layers.
※ Tip

Sending to Video media alone does not place the image on the timeline.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Exported images are rendered afresh from the edits and do not inherit the original image's EXIF, GPS, or camera information. However, this does not automatically remove faces, addresses, or screen information visible in the image.

Reimporting a finished image does not restore text and decoration as their original separate layers. Keep a .multina-image too if revisions are planned.

Project data includes media and additional fonts. Check image and font redistribution terms before giving it to someone else.

The canvas background, layer visibility/opacity, and whole-image effects are reflected in the finished image. Chroma-key inspection backgrounds and selection handles are excluded.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools19Image keys and troubleshootingOpenClose

Use “Shortcut settings” to view, add, change, or clear current keys.

  1. You can also open settings by right-clicking supported buttons or registered asset cards.
  2. The settings list separates standard actions from added assets. The table below shows the defaults.
  3. If a key does not work, check text input, dialogs, active tools, selection, and locks.
KeyDefault action
W A S DPan the canvas view. Supports holding the keys.
H / KHand / fit to view
Ctrl + wheel / middle-button dragZoom / pan the view
T / P / OAdd text / Marker / Eraser
M / BArea Mosaic / Area Blur
F / GLayer panel / cycle through the right-hand tabs
Y / U / IOpen Media / Presets / Custom
LOpen saved layers
C / V (also with Ctrl)Copy selected layers / paste into new layers
Ctrl+D / Delete / BackspaceDuplicate / delete selected layers
Ctrl+A / EscSelect all visible, unlocked layers / clear selection
Arrow keysMove selected layers by 1px
Z / XUndo / redo
JToggle focused view
Ctrl+SSave
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If changing color has no effect, check the target layer, effect ON/OFF state, and whether the changed setting applies to that asset.

Link to this explanation
Left · Assets20Choose image canvas dimensions and backgroundOpenClose

Canvas settings determine the finished image’s width, height, and transparency or background color. These are separate from viewing zoom.

  1. Open “Canvas settings” at the upper left and enter width and height in px. Match your purpose, for example 1280 × 720 for a landscape thumbnail or 1080 × 1920 for a portrait image.
  2. Choose a transparent background or a background color. To preserve transparency in output, use PNG／WebP. JPEG cannot store transparency.
  3. The initial automatic-size mode fits the first image placed. Once dimensions are changed manually, the first image no longer resizes the canvas automatically.
  4. Resizing changes only the canvas area, not the size of individual layers. If edges are cut off, adjust layer positioning and scale.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The limits are 8192px per side and 32 million pixels in total. Check the width and height combination too.

Display zoom makes the editing view easier to use; canvas dimensions determine the finished image’s pixel count. Images have no video fps setting.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas21Choose between copying layers and copying an imageOpenClose

You can copy editable layers or copy one flattened image.

  1. Select the target layer and right-click “Copy”. Pasting adds a new layer whose text content and decoration remain editable.
  2. To make one image of the visible result, use “Copy entire canvas as image”. After pasting, it is not separated into the original individual layers.
  3. Import an image copied outside the app with Media’s “Add from clipboard”, then place it on the canvas from the list.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

For long-term retention of a layer arrangement, register it in Saved layers; for a whole project, export a .multina-image. Do not use the clipboard as your only project storage.

Link to this explanation
