recording.title: Recording | Multina User Manual
recording.body:
Go to explanation
MultinaUser Manual
Featured featuresWorkflow tipsExplanation listInstallationTerms of use
Home›Recording

Recording

Capture your screen
and sound together

Record, then start creating!

Read explanation

Choose a feature that interests you

9 items
Top · Controls01Start recording!OpenClose

Check the source, save location, and audio, then try a short recording first.

  1. Choose a recording source and set the save location, recording name, saved size, and fps. Selecting these does not start recording.
  2. Turn on the system audio and microphone you need, then use the preview and audio meters to check the picture and sound.
  3. Start a short recording and wait for saving to finish after stopping. Play the finished file to check framing, motion, and audio before the real recording.
※ Tip

F9 stops recording while you use another app. It is registered only after recording starts.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The default stop key while using another app is F9. It is registered after recording starts and released on completion or interruption. If key registration fails, use the stop control in the Recording workspace.

Link to this explanation
Recording source02Choose the screen to recordOpenClose

Choose the entire screen or a specific window. Check for anything unintentionally visible too.

  1. Choose an entire screen or a window in the list on the left. If a newly opened app is missing, refresh the list with R, “Update”.
  2. Use P for preview and check the source and framing. Set the window size before recording starts.
  3. GPU window recording supports WGC／BitBlt. Entire-screen capture uses WGC. Capture-method changes apply to the next recording.
  4. If BitBlt produces a black picture or excessive load, stop and run a short WGC test. The source cannot be changed during recording.
※ Tip

The source and window size cannot be changed during recording.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Changing sources or resizing the captured window during recording is not supported. Set the size before starting.

BitBlt is a window-only alternative for comparison. Normal preview uses the existing method, so also check the saved file for the recording result.

The previous frame may be held when input stops updating. Minimizing the target or a frozen screen does not mean recording automatically pauses too.

Link to this explanation
Preview03Choose preview quality independently!OpenClose

Ultra-light, Lightweight, and Clear are checking qualities. They do not change the recorded file’s quality.

  1. Before starting, select Ultra-light / Lightweight / Clear above the preview button. This is separate from saved quality, and the selection is retained for next time.
  2. Use Ultra-light to prioritize performance or Clear to inspect small text. GPU recording preview is limited to 30fps.
  3. Stop display with V or Display ON／OFF. During GPU recording, this stops generating the shared preview while recording and audio continue.
  4. If excessive load is detected, the preview may return to Ultra-light for that recording. CPU-compatible recording handles preview differently from the GPU quality selector.
※ Tip

GPU preview is limited to 30fps. CPU recording uses a different method.

QualityApproximate preview limit
Ultra-light640 × 360
Lightweight960 × 540
Clear1280 × 720
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

GPU recording preview runs at up to 30fps. Recording at 100 / 120fps does not display the preview at the same fps.

If load is detected during GPU recording, the preview may revert to Ultra Light for that recording. Minimizing or turning display OFF stops shared preview generation.

Compatibility Recording (CPU) previews the same video used for recording. GPU preview-quality choices are unavailable. Display OFF does not stop capture or compression for recording itself.

Even with display OFF, recording, audio processing, and necessary status displays still use resources.

Link to this explanation
Recording settings04Check PC sound and microphoneOpenClose

Turn system audio and microphone ON／OFF separately. Include only the sound you need.

  1. Before starting, turn on only the required system audio and microphone inputs. Choose the microphone input device too.
  2. Start preview, play some sound, and check the sound-detected indicator and meters. Audio is not played back through the speakers for monitoring.
  3. System-audio and microphone volume ranges are 0–200%, with 100% as the baseline. Volume can change during recording, but devices and audio ON／OFF states cannot.
  4. Use a short file to check for doubled audio, silence, or distortion. Microphone ON is not retained after restarting; check it each time.
※ Tip

System audio includes playback from the entire PC, not only the selected window.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Only volume can be changed during recording. Audio ON/OFF, the microphone device, and the source cannot change. Stop and reconfigure if necessary.

The microphone input device selection is retained, but Microphone ON is not carried over after restarting the app. Check it before recording.

During preview, you can switch microphones while keeping the video. Microphone OFF stops only microphone capture.

There is no audio monitoring playback. Not hearing your microphone through the speakers does not by itself mean the recording is silent.

System audio uses Windows loopback and includes playback across the PC, not only the selected window. Check notification sounds and similar sources beforehand.

If System Audio is ON but no audio track can be acquired, recording is prevented from starting and a message appears. Reselect the source, or turn System Audio OFF if unnecessary, then retry.

Link to this explanation
Recording settings05Saved size, fps, and qualityOpenClose

Before starting, choose Original size / Full HD / WQHD / 4K and 30／60／100／120fps.

  1. Choose Original size / Full HD / WQHD / 4K. The picture is reduced while retaining its aspect ratio; smaller sources are not enlarged.
  2. Choose 30／60／100／120fps for your purpose and system load. The default 100fps is not guaranteed to be stable on every PC.
  3. If GPU support is unavailable, manually select compatible recording (CPU) if needed. Recording does not switch automatically from GPU to CPU.
  4. Choose High quality / Maximum quality (large files) / Custom. Custom supports 4–300Mbps. Compare file size and motion reproduction using short saved files.
※ Tip

The default 100fps does not mean it is recommended for every PC.

EncoderWhen to use it
Native GPU (automatic selection)Chooses an available GPU recording method. Captures directly from Windows and scales/compresses to H.264 on the GPU.
Native GPU (stop if unsupported)Requires GPU support to start. If unsupported, recording does not start; check the error.
Compatibility recording (CPU)An explicitly selected compatibility method for cases such as an unavailable GPU method. Check processing load and the saved result with a short recording.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The default 100fps is not a recommendation for every PC or purpose. Try 30 / 60fps too, according to motion, workload, and storage needs.

Maximum saved dimensions are 1920×1080 for Full HD, 2560×1440 for WQHD, and 3840×2160 for 4K. Vertical and other sources produce different dimensions to preserve aspect ratio.

Native GPU uses a constant-bitrate target; compatibility recording uses variable bitrate. Highest Quality still uses lossy compression and is not lossless.

If you will edit afterward, matching recording, video-project, and export fps helps avoid frame dropping caused by differing frame rates.

Link to this explanation
Recording settings06Monitor recording statusOpenClose

Input fps and encoded fps are different. A still screen may be normal even with few input updates.

  1. Input fps describes image capture; encoded fps describes compression. Low input activity on a still screen may be normal.
  2. If input stays low even on a moving screen, check capture load and the target app’s load. If more queued frames are dropped, review processing load.
  3. Compare with preview OFF or Ultra-light. If this does not help, stop and review size, fps, and recording method. Check the finished file, not just statistics.
DisplayMeaning
Input fpsActual capture/update activity. For BitBlt, this is the capture count, not the game's internal fps.
Encoded fpsCalculated from the number of compressed frames. Includes frames that reuse the same image.
Identical frames reusedThe number of times the previous image was recorded again, such as when input did not update. No new motion was generated.
Queued frames droppedThe number of waiting frames discarded. Reassess load if it increases.
MB processedAmount of data processed. This is not confirmation that the final file has finished saving.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Statistics do not guarantee a successful recording. Play the saved file and check motion and audio synchronization.

Read warnings if the recording source or audio device stops. Subsequent audio may be missing, so check the device and stop recording.

Link to this explanation
Top · Controls07After stopping, wait for saving to finishOpenClose

The initial save location is Downloads. Change it before recording.

  1. Stop with the Stop button, Space, or registered F9.
  2. After finalization, check the duration, ending, and audio.
  3. To edit the recording, import the saved MP4 in the Video workspace.
! Caution

Do not force quit or disconnect the save location while saving is in progress.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Warnings such as Save Received Recording or Check Partial File may indicate a missing ending. Inspect such files separately from completed recordings.

Recovery is not guaranteed after destination disconnection, insufficient space, or force-closing. Test before important recordings.

Link to this explanation
Recording settings08Checks for long recordingsOpenClose

Check free space, GPU load, and audio devices, and test in the same environment beforehand.

  1. If playback stutters, compare with preview OFF or Ultra-light.
  2. If a warning or stop occurs, check its message, time, and the saved file’s ending.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Do not force-close the app or disconnect the destination during recording or finalization. Recovery cannot be guaranteed.

Link to this explanation
Top · Controls09Customize your recording keysOpenClose

View, change, or clear assignments in “Shortcut settings”. You can also change them by right-clicking supported buttons.

  1. Add, change, or clear assignments in “Shortcut settings”. Right-clicking a supported button also opens settings for that action.
  2. Normal keys work while the Recording workspace has focus. Text entry or dialogs may take priority.
  3. F9 is registered only after recording starts and is released when recording ends. If another app already uses it, it may be unavailable, so also locate the Stop button.
  4. “Open saved recording location” and “Cancel preparation” have no default keys; assign them if needed. Canceling preparation is different from stopping an active recording.
KeyAction
SpaceStart / stop recording (in app)
F9Stop recording (only while recording; also works in other apps)
PStart / stop preview
VToggle preview display ON / OFF
RRefresh sources
DChange save folder
SShortcut settings
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

F9 is a stop key registered after recording starts and released on completion or interruption. If registration fails, for example because another app uses it, use the on-screen stop button.

Normal keys such as Space, P, and V work while the Recording workspace is active. Text entry may take priority in input fields and settings dialogs.

Open Saved Recording Location and “Cancel recording/preview preparation” have no default key. Assign them in shortcut settings if needed. Canceling preparation differs from stopping an active recording normally.

Link to this explanation

No matching items

comic.title: Comics · Illustration | Multina User Manual
comic.body:
Go to explanation
MultinaUser Manual
Featured featuresWorkflow tipsExplanation listInstallationTerms of use
Home›Comics · Illustration

Comics · Illustration

Comics and illustrations:
enjoy drawing them

Tell stories with pens and panels!

Read explanation
Comic & Illustration is a prototype

Choose a feature that interests you

33 items
Top · Tools01Create your first document!OpenClose

Choose the project name, document type, size, and DPI, then select a drawing layer for finished lines.

  1. In an empty tab, set the project name, Comic / Illustration / Vertical comic, width, height, and DPI. For print work, check the required dimensions first.
  2. From the initial draft and drawing layers, select the drawing layer for finished work. Draft layers are excluded from finished output.
  3. Press Q to switch to the pen and try its color, thickness, and opacity. Use “Add with paper settings” for pages with different dimensions.
※ Tip

The initial page has draft and drawing layers. Draft layers are not included in finished output.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

DPI determines printed size. With the same pixel count, changing DPI changes physical paper dimensions. For print work, decide the required pixels and DPI first.

Draft and hidden layers are excluded from PNG / PDF. New-document fields allow 64–16384px per side and 36–1200 DPI. Total-pixel and operation-specific limits also apply, so not every feature is necessarily available on large documents.

Link to this explanation
Left · Document / Media02Set up a comfortable drawing workspaceOpenClose

Show or hide panels and drag their boundaries to adjust width.

  1. Use the view buttons at the top to show or hide panels, and drag the left/right boundaries to adjust width. Focused view with R gives the canvas more room.
  2. Adjust pressure, stabilization, and softness in the drawing-feel controls on the left. Stronger stabilization also changes tracking response, so start with small values.
  3. White/checkerboard controls how transparent areas are displayed, not the PNG background. “Entire manuscript” fits the paper to the screen; J returns to 100%.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Stronger stabilization also changes how the line follows your hand. Start with a low value and test at your actual drawing speed.

Changing the app language does not bulk-change existing dialogue, project names, layer names, or text formatting you have adjusted.

Link to this explanation
Left · Document / Media03Document color, crop marks, and spreadsOpenClose

Set expression color and guides in Document on the left. Guides are excluded from finished output.

  1. Choose Color / Gray / Monochrome and Right / Left / Spread.
  2. Adjust bleed and safe-frame margins.
※ Tip

Changing expression color does not batch-convert existing pixels.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Expression color affects subsequent drawing colors; it does not bulk-convert existing pixels or transparency. The expression-color field cannot be changed for image layers.

Blue indicates trim/crop marks and purple the safe frame. Margins shrink automatically on small paper. Guides are excluded from finished output.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas04Pan, zoom, and rotateOpenClose

Pan with WASD or the hand tool. Rotate the view to a comfortable drawing angle.

  1. Press J for 100%. Zoom using the zoom control or Ctrl＋wheel.
  2. Choose a rotation increment, rotate with Alt＋A／D, and return to 0° with Alt＋W.
  3. Press R for focused view. Space＋drag is available when enabled in settings.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Keys may be unavailable during text entry or dialog interaction to prevent accidental actions.

Link to this explanation
Page list05Pages, images, and artwork flipsOpenClose

Add or duplicate pages and insert images on separate layers.

  1. Adding creates a new page; duplicating carries over the source page’s contents. Right-click a page to duplicate or delete it, and use K／L to move to the previous/next page.
  2. Press M to switch Document/Media and import image copies. Insertion creates a new layer. Choose Artwork image or Tracing draft.
  3. 1 flips the entire current page horizontally. Vertical flipping also changes the whole page’s contents and is reflected in saves and exports.
  4. Right-click flipping within a selection affects only the enclosed area of that layer. Distinguish this scope from flipping the entire page.
※ Tip

Artwork flips affect saves and exports too. They are not merely a mirrored view.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Artwork flips also affect text and images and are reflected in saving/export. Distinguish them from view rotation for inspection, and undo if unintended.

Artwork Image (Normal) fits within the document without enlarging beyond its original size and is centered. Tracing is inserted sized to the document.

Unlock the target layer to edit an image. Its original file is not directly rewritten.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements06Choose each layer’s roleOpenClose

Drawing layers hold colors and lines, vector layers manage strokes, and panel layers are exclusively for panel operations.

  1. Check lock and visibility states; right-click to rename, duplicate, or delete.
  2. Drag to change stacking order. The ↑／↓ keys move the layer selection.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Panel layers are exclusively for panel operations. Do not use them as targets for pens, erasers, text, or similar content.

When using clipping, pay attention to the relationship with the base layer too.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements07The whole layer, or an element inside it?OpenClose

Select and adjust a layer separately from text, shapes, and other elements inside it.

  1. ← opens Layers; → opens Element / Panel Settings. Adjust the whole layer separately from its text, shapes, and other elements.
  2. Opacity, blending, and fx apply per layer. To change an element’s text or pattern, select that element in the element list.
  3. Clipping limits visibility to a base layer’s shape. Check whether the base is automatic or specified, as well as visibility and stacking order.
  4. Keep a duplicate before rasterizing or merging down. Afterward, you may lose individual editing of text content, patterns, or vectors.
! Caution

Rasterizing removes text, pattern, and vector editability.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Merging requires visible layers with Normal blending and matching draft status. Panel layers or layers involved in clipping cannot be merged/rasterized directly.

Clipping can use an automatic shared base or a specified lower layer. Multilevel relationships using an already clipped layer as a base are also supported. Check base relationships when reordering.

Stroke-width and stroke-color changes in vector details apply to every stroke on that layer. They do not edit just one stroke.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements08Recolor only what you have drawnOpenClose

This protects transparency on the same layer. Use it to recolor existing lines or fills.

  1. Turn it ON only while recoloring. Return it to OFF for normal drawing or erasing.
  2. Use clipping to follow a base layer’s shape on a separate layer.
※ Tip

While ON, you cannot draw in empty areas or use the eraser.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

While ON, you cannot draw in transparent areas or use the eraser. Check this setting if nothing appears on a transparent layer.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools09Choose a pen with the feel you wantOpenClose

Choose among 25 standard pens for lines, mixing and textures, or lettering and patterns.

  1. Choose the pen type, thickness, opacity, and color.
  2. Try variations in line weight and mixing with underlying colors.
※ Tip

Test pixel mixing and color spreading on a drawing layer.

TypeSuggested uses
G-Pen / Mapping PenPressure-sensitive line width. Start with G-Pen for expressive finished lines and Mapping Pen for fine detail.
FinelinerDraws uniform lines without pressure-based width changes at the default settings.
Ink pooling penLines with ink pooling. Test the appearance of pauses and overlaps.
PencilDrafting and shading with grain and pressure-sensitive opacity.
Flat Marker / Square PenFlat-tip strokes and square strokes unaffected by pressure.
Airbrush: Soft / Light Broad Paint / BlendSoft spraying, broad pale color, and blending with color mixing.
HighlighterA flat pen for layering translucent color.
Ink Brush: Calligraphy / DryBrush lines using width variation, bristle marks, and ink depletion.
Opaque Paint: Flat Brush / Soft BrushPaints while mixing with the underlying color. Choose flat or soft brush marks.
Watercolor · Light washTranslucent paint, bleeding, pigment variation, and edge pooling.
Oil · Dry flat brushFlat-brush bristle marks and color spreading.
Charcoal · RoughShadows and texture with grain and broken marks.
Lettering Pen: Round / Pointed / SquareHand lettering that joins the outer edges of overlapping strokes for outlining.
Special Pen: Sparkle / HeartPlaces image tips at regular intervals.
Special Pen: Hatching (Diagonal Cross) / (Grid)Draws diagonal or horizontal/vertical grids. Adjust dedicated line width, spacing, and overlap settings.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Test on a drawing layer when pixel mixing and color spreading matter. Vector layers retain strokes; not every brush medium gives the same result as raster drawing.

The airbrush cursor circle indicates its dense center. Faint edges may extend outside the circle.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools10The 4 pen-settings tabsOpenClose

Adjust basics, color mixing, pen tip, and edge/pressure while testing.

  1. Use Basic to adjust thickness, opacity, tapering, and more. “Color mixing” controls pickup of underlying colors, spreading, and bleeding with ON／OFF switches and numeric values.
  2. In “Pen tip”, adjust shape, image assets, spacing, scattering, and more. In “Edge · Pressure”, adjust edges and pressure response. The table below lists the settings.
  3. Try thin lines, thick lines, and overlapping strokes on the test canvas. For temporary use choose “Use these settings”; to reuse them later, give them a name and register them.
TabSettings and checks
BasicNormal Pen / Asset Pen, base pen, size, opacity, and test color.
Fill · Color mixingMedium, softness, color mixing, mixing amount, color spread, bleeding, paint amount, flow, and grain. Watercolor and charcoal also offer pigment variation and per-stroke pattern changes; watercolor adds edge pooling, while ink brushes add bristle/dry marks and ink depletion.
Texture DetailsInk pooling, tip interaction with paper, and flat-brush bristles. Test in combination with size and color.
Pen tipHatching, round / square-flat / star, image asset, aspect ratio, angle, spacing, and scatter.
Edge · PressurePressure ON, minimum pressure width, pressure curve, pressure opacity, tapering, and outline method. Set color, width, and blur for 2 outlines; width 0 turns one OFF.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Turning Color Mixing or Bleeding OFF disables the corresponding adjustments. Retained values have no effect unless the feature is ON.

Pressure Opacity 0 gives constant opacity. Tapering is mainly for mouse use; pen input prioritizes actual pressure.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools11Register your own penOpenClose

Pen type → “Custom settings…”. Give it a name, test it, and register it.

  1. Open “Pen type” → “Custom settings…” and choose a base pen and name. Changing the base pen replaces the settings being edited.
  2. Adjust each tab and test the feel on the unsaved test canvas on the right. You can also assign a recall key; avoid conflicts.
  3. Use “Use these settings” temporarily or “Register” for a persistent addition. For an existing pen, choose “Save changes” or “Register with another name” as appropriate.
  4. Import .multinapen or supported GBR files. Right-click added pens to edit, change their key, delete to the Recycle Bin, or export them.
! Caution

ABR, SUT, and KPP are not supported. Check which formats can be imported.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Use These Settings alone does not permanently register an additional pen. Register it or save changes to use it next time.

Import supports .multinapen (or .json with compatible contents) and GBR v2 grayscale/RGBA image brushes. Settings files may be up to 8MB; GBR up to 32MB. ABR, SUT, and KPP are unsupported. GBR import does not inherit another app's proprietary mixing engine.

Delete additional pens through “Delete (to Recycle Bin)” in the context menu. This moves the app's dedicated settings/assets, leaving the import source unchanged. If a device assignment recalled the deleted pen, choose a new assignment too.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools12Asset pens and connected lettering pensOpenClose

Use asset pens with image-based tips and lettering pens that combine the outside edges of strokes.

  1. Load an image as an asset pen’s tip and choose its original colors or tinting with the drawing color. Even large source images are drawn at the configured tip size.
  2. Adjust regular/random placement, spacing, and scattering. This tool places patterns rather than drawing an ordinary continuous line.
  3. The lettering pen’s Connected outline joins the exterior without drawing borders between overlapping strokes. Choose round, pointed, or square tips.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Use Connected Outline when adding an outline to an asset pen.

Switching between lettering pens and normal drawing may create a separate drawing layer to preserve outlines. Check the newly selected layer.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas13Hold to straighten a lineOpenClose

Draw a pen stroke and pause at the endpoint for about 1 second without releasing to straighten that stroke.

  1. Keep holding at the endpoint; once the stroke becomes straight, adjust its position and release.
  2. If it changes unintentionally, undo with Z.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

This affects the current stroke only. It does not straighten multiple earlier strokes at once. It differs from erasing or adjusting rulers.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools14Erase, erase to intersections, or smudgeOpenClose

E is the ordinary eraser. The intersection eraser is vector-only. Smudge spreads color.

  1. Select the target layer, then choose hard, soft, or kneaded eraser, thickness, and opacity. E is the ordinary eraser that removes the parts you touch.
  2. “Intersection eraser” trims selected vector lines up to intersections. Its removal range differs from ordinary E, so try a short stroke first.
  3. Smudge spreads color using its own size and mixing settings. It blends with underlying color rather than erasing.
  4. When Restore erased areas appears for an image or element, it restores all erasure information for that target. This differs from Z, which undoes the last action.
※ Tip

Panel layers, locks, transparency protection, selections, and other conditions restrict actions.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Locks, visibility, transparency protection, selections, and panel assignments restrict editing. Panel layers cannot be erased. To conceal a border artistically, use a drawing layer above it.

Restore Erased Areas differs from undoing with Z. It removes all stored erasure on the target. Restoration is not always possible, for example after conversion to a drawing.

The original image file is unchanged. However, the edited result within the document is saved in the project.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas15Fill, enclose, and edit regionsOpenClose

F is Fill bucket, H is Enclosed fill, and G is Selection.

  1. F is Fill bucket, H is Enclosed fill, and G is Selection. Choose a visible, unlocked drawing layer as the fill destination.
  2. Set the bucket’s reference layer, tolerance, and expansion under lines. You can refer to separate line art while filling on the selected layer.
  3. Create a rectangular or freehand selection with G to limit drawing, filling, and erasing to that region. Clear it with Esc.
  4. Right-click inside the selection for delete, flip, copy to a new layer, and other actions. Separating and transforming a region may rasterize the selected layer.
! Caution

An enclosed selection targets only the selected layer. Region transformation may rasterize it.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Some selection-editing actions rasterize the selected layer. To retain editable text and shapes, duplicate the layer or save the project first. Original image files are retained, and you can undo immediately afterward.

Operations that rasterize the whole document, such as Bucket, support up to 8 million pixels. Use Cancel Fill while filling is in progress.

An area selection does not select multiple layers at once. Always check which layer is selected.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements16Move the whole layer or one elementOpenClose

Tap Shift to move or transform an entire layer. Moving individual elements uses a different tool.

  1. Tap Shift or use Move/Transform to display the whole-layer frame. Move, scale, or rotate, then press again to finish.
  2. For just one text or shape element, choose the individual-element move tool. Distinguish the whole-layer frame from a single-element selection.
  3. Turn right-click “Edit crop” ON to narrow the area to keep. Turn it OFF to finish editing; turn “Apply crop” OFF to compare with the uncropped version.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Cropping specifies what is visible; it differs from Eraser or Delete Area. Turning off editing mode does not necessarily disable the crop result.

Distinguish holding Shift while pressing another key from tapping Shift alone to switch tools.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements17Adjust shapes and textOpenClose

New-drawing settings apply to the next placement. To change an existing element, select it and edit it.

  1. Choose a tool, line, and fill, then drag on the canvas to place it.
  2. For text, adjust content, typeface, direction, and outline.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Content is limited to 2000 characters per element. Divide long text into readable units rather than packing it into one element.

New non-Japanese text defaults to a supported font and horizontal writing. Switching languages does not overwrite existing content or user-selected formatting.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements18Apply screentones and hatchingOpenClose

T is Tone; Y is Tone bucket. Adjust pattern, spacing, density, and more afterward.

  1. T selects Tone and Y selects Tone bucket. In New drawing settings, choose pattern, spacing, density, size, angle, and more, then apply by enclosure, pen, rectangle, or bucket.
  2. Select existing tones in the element list to change them. “Continue painting with this pattern” affects the next placement; All tones on the same layer aligns settings across that layer.
  3. The hatching pen has its own line width, spacing, angle, and irregularity. Right-click to choose no overlap or overlap, determining whether patterns align or accumulate.
  4. Fine patterns may show moiré when zoomed out. Check display suppression settings separately from output at the original pixel dimensions.
※ Tip

Tone regions on the same layer are replaced by patterns applied later.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Tone areas on the same layer are replaced by subsequently applied patterns rather than stacking tones. Different layers use normal compositing.

No Overlap aligns hatching patterns; “With overlap” changes the pattern position per stroke so strokes can fill gaps. It does not simply increase dot density within one stroke.

Frequency in lpi and spacing in px are linked by document DPI. Fine patterns may appear as an averaged shade when zoomed out. Check using “Screentone moiré reduction”, 100% view, and the actual PNG as appropriate.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools19Divide panels and extend them to the edgeOpenClose

Create borders with O and divide panels with P. Diagonal splits and panel adjustments are supported too.

  1. Creating a panel border with O creates a dedicated panel layer. Divide with P, and use diagonal splitting or panel adjustment to change vertices and shapes.
  2. Right-click inside a panel and toggle Extend to top edge or similar options ON／OFF. The edge is the document edge, not merely the inside of the trim boundary.
  3. Draw artwork on a separate drawing layer. Panel layers are only for border operations, not for pens, erasers, text, or similar content.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

New artwork is confined to panels by default. For intentional overflow, explicitly select the target layer and adjust the setting.

Create artwork on a separate drawing layer instead of using Pen or Eraser on a panel layer. Place artwork covering a frame on a layer above it too.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements20Inside panels and breaking out of themOpenClose

Panel assignment keeps artwork inside one panel. Draw in front of the border on a separate layer.

  1. Panel interiors are transparent. For each page, choose the default white cover or transparency outside panels. Also check the drawing layer’s panel assignment.
  2. “Panel assignment” keeps artwork inside one panel. Check the assignment after adjusting panels too.
  3. Use “Draw in front of panel borders” for breakout effects. It is OFF by default; explicitly turn it ON only for targets that should cross the border.
  4. To remove only a border, right-click “Delete border only (keep artwork)”. To hide a border with white paint, use a drawing layer above it.
※ Tip

New drawing is not allowed to cross borders by default. Manage borders and artwork separately.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

A locked panel layer prevents frame adjustment and similar operations. You do not draw on a panel layer with normal Pen or Eraser tools.

Panel gaps range from 0–200px. This is separate from print margins in mm and guide bleed.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools21Put dialogue in speech balloonsOpenClose

U is Speech balloon; I is Text. Choose content, shape, white/transparent fill, and text direction first.

  1. Choose the placement area on the document and check the margins around the dialogue.
  2. To revise an existing item, select that element and edit it.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

New Japanese speech bubbles default to vertical writing; other languages default to horizontal. Change this to suit the project.

Adjust Impact, Cloud, and Spiky Flash bubbles to suit the amount of text and frame proportions.

Link to this explanation
Right · Layers / Elements22Fine-tune shapes and tailsOpenClose

Choose cloud-like, dramatic, spiky burst, and other shapes to match the tone of the dialogue.

  1. Set the body shape, width, height, irregularity, and type while leaving margins around the dialogue. Select an existing element before changing it.
  2. Use “Move tail” and drag the blue base or orange tip. You can also edit tail direction, length, width, and curve numerically.
  3. Choose thought bubbles or no tail when appropriate to the scene. Finish tail editing with the button on the right or Esc.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Tail width is based on the body's shorter side. Length/width sliders and numeric fields have different limits; numeric fields allow a wider range.

Tail controls are not shown for every shape. Not all decorative bubbles can have a regular tail.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas23Rulers: adjust, draw, or turn OFFOpenClose

Rulers are shared by all layers on the current page. After positioning one, switch to Drawing.

  1. Choosing a type starts in adjustment mode. Move points, triangles, hexagons, or frames; you can also enter angles, centers, and other values numerically.
  2. Switch to “Drawing” to draw along the guides. Selecting a tool with Q or another key while adjusting returns the ruler to Drawing.
  3. “OFF” hides the ruler and returns to free drawing while retaining its position. Pressing Q while it is OFF does not reactivate it automatically.
  4. With rulers OFF, right-click targeting returns to artwork, selections, and panels. Use “Entire ruler” to inspect distant vanishing points.
※ Tip

OFF retains the position. “None” removes the ruler type.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Ruler angles are measured on the document. Do not confuse them with rotation of the displayed canvas.

Right-clicking perspective guides or while a center ruler is active also offers ruler options. If the artwork or panel target is unclear, turn the ruler OFF temporarily.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas24Perspective, center, and symmetry rulersOpenClose

Perspective rulers lead toward vanishing points; center rulers lead toward the center. Rulers for curves and symmetrical lines are also available.

  1. Choose 1／2／3-point perspective in the perspective field or by right-clicking a supported guide. Triangles are vanishing points, the 2 round points define the horizontal reference, and hexagons shift reference lines in parallel.
  2. Vanishing points can be outside the document. Zoom out or use “Entire ruler” to inspect them, then switch to Drawing after adjustment.
  3. A stroke locks to the axis nearest its starting direction. To use another axis, lift the pen and start again. Cross rulers provide horizontal/vertical lines; symmetry rulers mirror strokes.
  4. An ellipse reference on a center ruler produces straight lines from its outline toward the center. Concentric ellipses produce curves. Separate handles adjust ellipse width and height.
RulerStroke behavior
Horizontal / VerticalStraight lines along the document's horizontal/vertical direction. Changing the angle makes it a straight/parallel-line ruler.
CrossLocks to the horizontal or vertical direction closest to the stroke's initial movement.
Straight / Parallel LinesParallel lines at the configured angle.
SymmetryMirrors pen strokes across an axis defined by center and angle.
1-Point PerspectiveToward 1 vanishing point, or parallel to the horizontal reference.
2-Point PerspectiveToward either of 2 vanishing points, or perpendicular to the line connecting them.
3-Point PerspectiveToward any of 3 vanishing points.
Center rulerA straight line from the pen's initial position toward the center. Right-click to switch Center Point / Ellipse Reference.
Concentric CirclesDraws an arc whose radius is the distance from the center to the pen's initial position.
Concentric EllipsesDraws an elliptical arc through the pen's initial position using the configured aspect ratio and angle.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Vanishing points can be outside the document. Numeric coordinates range from −32768 to 32768. Use Fit Entire Ruler if you lose sight of them.

The symmetry ruler mirrors pen strokes across its axis. Eraser and Smudge remain freehand without mirrored copies. The default axis angle is 90°; change it if needed.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas25Add impact with focus lines!OpenClose

Right-click inside a panel to target it, or use the whole document when there is no target panel.

  1. Right-click inside a panel to add focus lines there; without a target, add them to the entire document. For angled panels, line ends follow the panel outline.
  2. In the temporary preview, adjust count, length, thickness, the central opening, and irregularity. Position the opening with the handle or horizontal/vertical sliders and numeric fields.
  3. “Confirm” adds a new focus-line layer. Cancel discards the temporary preview. Later, right-click “Adjust focus lines” to revise them.
Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas26Revise focus lines laterOpenClose

Right-click “Adjust focus lines” to change count, thickness, opening position, and irregularity.

  1. Drag the handle or use numeric position values to align the opening.
  2. Setting the opening’s width or height to 0 removes the opening.
  3. Change the pattern to vary the irregularity, then confirm to apply.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The dot and dashed lines are excluded from export. For angled panels, check that line ends follow the boundary.

Focus lines can be erased. To add pen strokes, add a separate drawing layer or rasterize with the understanding that editability will be lost.

Link to this explanation
Center · Canvas27Comic right-click actions at a glanceOpenClose

Available actions depend on the tool, location, selection, and layer.

LocationMain actions
Standard pen type fieldOpen Custom Settings from the current settings.
Additional pen type fieldEdit / Key Settings; Delete (Move to Recycle Bin).
Hatching type field / dedicated settingsAllow Overlap / No Overlap. The type field also opens Custom Settings.
Perspective ruler field / corresponding guides1- / 2- / 3-point perspective.
Center ruler field / active center rulerCenter Point / Ellipse Reference.
Move / Transform buttonToggle crop editing.
Inside a canvas selectionDelete area, flip, edit crop, and more.
Panel on the canvasExtend to Edge, Delete Frame Only, add focus lines.
Element / layer on the canvasDelete target, flip, crop, adjust focus lines, and more.
Layer cardRename, duplicate, flip horizontally/vertically, delete, and readjust focus lines.
Page buttonDuplicate / delete.
Project tabRename project; save and remove from tab.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Inside a selection, “Selected area” actions take priority. Actions are disabled for locked targets and similar conditions. Click outside or press Esc to close the menu without acting.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools28Tablets and one-handed controllersOpenClose

These settings are specific to Comic & Illustration. Assign functions to the keys sent by the driver.

  1. Use the manufacturer’s controls to check the device, display connection, and pen input.
  2. Register and test buttons, dials, and pressure in Device settings.
※ Tip

This does not directly recognize every manufacturer’s proprietary USB signals.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

This does not directly recognize every manufacturer's proprietary USB signals. It uses key assignments supplied by the driver.

Testing on actual devices and individual models is not complete. Try settings that do not conflict with normal keys.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools29Button, dial, and pressure settingsOpenClose

Pen-side buttons can also be registered by sending keys. Settings are shared across all comic projects.

  1. Enable the device, add buttons or pen-side buttons, and register both the input key sent by the driver and the action to call.
  2. For a dial, set left/right input keys, action, sensitivity, and reverse rotation. Choose keys that do not conflict with normal shortcuts.
  3. Use test drawing to compare raw and adjusted pressure. Turning touch drawing OFF still allows pen and mouse use.
  4. Working monitor sets where the app moves. Configure a pen display’s video connection and coordinate calibration in the manufacturer’s software or Windows, then finish with “Save settings”.
※ Tip

Working monitor moves the app. It is separate from a pen display’s video connection or coordinate calibration.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Each category has 20 button slots and 8 dial slots. Use different keys when registering alternate driver modes too.

Duplicate keys within the same settings screen and conflicts with additional-pen recall keys are checked on save. Disabling an assignment does not erase its name or settings.

Resetting a category's assignments removes its comic button/dial mappings while retaining artwork, additional pens, and pressure settings. Reset Pressure to Default is separate.

A driver assignment to right-click opens the normal context menu. To assign a custom action instead, change the driver to send a key.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools30Use saving and history for different purposesOpenClose

Autosave preserves edits; the Save button also creates a history entry at a milestone.

  1. Pause and check for “Saved”. Ctrl＋S performs a normal save.
  2. Use the Save button to retain history. Restore the latest 3 entries from Project list.
※ Tip

If a save-failure message appears, investigate the cause before closing.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If saving fails, edits are retained and an error appears. Do not exit while Unsaved Changes or Save Failed remains; check the destination and error.

Undo / Redo is the current editing history; Save History contains manually saved versions; .mcomic is editable data exported elsewhere. They do not replace one another.

For projects marked Recoverable or Needs Review because of damage or similar issues, check their status and content in the list. A recovery label alone does not prove every asset is intact.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools31PNG, print PDF, and editable dataOpenClose

Both PNG and PDF support All pages / Current page. The default is All pages. Use .mcomic to take editable work elsewhere.

  1. Choose PNG in finished-output “Export” and check the page range and white/transparent background.
  2. Press “Export” and choose a destination folder. Pages are saved as 001.png, 002.png… in a new folder named after the project. Existing output with the same name is not overwritten.
  3. Each page retains its pixel dimensions and DPI. Draft and hidden layers, rulers, and guides are excluded.
  4. For general-purpose print PDF, check dimensions in mm and page order, then print at actual size / 100%.
  5. For editable pages, layers, and assets, use project “Export” to create a .mcomic. Use “Import” to load it into a new project.
! Caution

PDF/X, CMYK, and printer-specific submission formats are not supported. Check the recipient’s requirements.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Output includes visible artwork, panel frames, and layer effects, excluding draft/hidden layers, editing guides, rulers, and adjustment handles.

Transparent PNG does not automatically make painted white or “Hide outside panels with white” transparent. Check the document's outside-panel setting if necessary.

PDF pages contain losslessly compressed RGB images on white backgrounds. They follow document pixel dimensions and each page's DPI; whole-document output records a TrimBox for the trim area. This is not a searchable-text PDF or a PDF preserving vector strokes.

CMYK, PDF/X, and print-shop-specific submission formats are unsupported. Crop marks are not printed. Physical printing and print-shop submission have not been fully tested, so compare required color, bleed, resolution, and format against the recipient's specifications.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools32Comic & Illustration is a prototypeOpenClose

Comic & Illustration is a prototype.

Link to this explanation
Top · Tools33Comic keys and troubleshooting drawingOpenClose

Check standard tool keys, added-pen keys, and device assignments separately.

  1. The table below lists standard keys. Register or change added-pen keys in Custom settings’ recall-key field or the pen’s right-click menu.
  2. Device settings map the keys sent by buttons or dials to Comic actions.
  3. Check visibility, locks, layer type, transparency protection, selection, and panel assignment. Set rulers to Drawing or OFF, and check for text input or dialogs.
KeyStandard action
W / A / S / DPan the view up / left / down / right
Q / EPen / normal Eraser
F / G / HBucket / Lasso Selection / Lasso Fill
B / NHand / Eyedropper from visible artwork
T / YTone / Tone Bucket
U / ISpeech Bubble / Text
O / PPanel Frame / Split Panel
Tap Shift aloneSwitch to Move / Transform
C / V or Ctrl+C / Ctrl+VCopy layer / selected area; paste as a new layer
Z / XUndo / redo
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+ZUndo / redo / redo
[ / ]Decrease / increase brush size
← / →Layers / Element & Panel Settings tab
↑ / ↓Select layer above / below
K / LPrevious / next page
M / R / JToggle Document / Media; focused view; 100% view
Alt+A / Alt+D / Alt+WRotate view left / right / reset to 0°
Top-row 1Flip current-page artwork horizontally
Ctrl + wheelZoom the view
Space + dragTemporarily pan when the setting is ON
EscDeselect or finish/cancel adjustments and menus (depends on current state)
Ctrl+SSave current edits. Use Save at the top to create a save-history entry
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Tapping Shift switches tools when the key is released. Distinguish this from other Shift actions or device assignments.

↑ / ↓ selects layers; it does not reorder them. Arrow buttons in the layer list change front/back stacking order.

App integration screen01What can AI integration do?OpenClose

Dedicated automatic insertion supports music videos and thumbnails. Creative discussions with an external AI are separate from applying results in the app.

  1. Discussing and generating assets with an external AI is separate from inserting editing data into the app. Automatic insertion supports music videos and thumbnails.
  2. Comic support currently covers planning, roughs, asset discussions, and recipe management. Dedicated automatic insertion for Edit, Materials, and Recipe is also not implemented.
  3. You can register original recipes even for modes still in preparation. Registering one alone does not enable automatic editing.
※ Tip

Comic support extends to planning discussions and recipe management. Features still in preparation, such as Edit and Materials, do not support automatic insertion.

ModeWorkspace / available scope in this version
MVVideo. Supports production requirements, applying an editing package, and completion after verification.
ThumbnailImage. Supports landscape/portrait requirements, applying an image recipe with independent layers, and checking the result.
EditVideo. Coming Soon. Integration/progress display and custom instruction management. Dedicated automatic editing is not implemented.
DocumentsImage. Coming Soon. Orientation choice, integration/progress display, and instruction management. Dedicated automatic insertion is not implemented.
ComicsComics & Illustration. Standard production guide, integration/progress display, and instruction management. Dedicated automatic insertion is not implemented.
RecipeSpecify Video, Image, or Comic as the current target. Cross-domain instruction management and integration display. General-purpose automatic insertion is not implemented.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

The app does not contain a built-in generative model. Available work and costs depend on the external AI's capabilities, connection environment, and subscription.

Only 1 AI mode can be connected at a time. Disconnect the current mode before switching. Merely opening this manual does not connect or transmit media.

Registering instructions for a Coming Soon mode does not enable automatic editing.

Link to this explanation
App integration screen02Ask the AI to connectOpenClose

You need an external AI environment capable of connecting to Multina on your PC.

  1. Prepare the target workspace and an empty tab in the app. Decide in advance whether to create new work or continue existing work.
  2. Ask the AI to read the supplied START_HERE.md. Music videos use resources/mv-mode, thumbnails use thumbnail-mode, and comics use comic-mode.
  3. Check the connection confirmation on the AI side and the connected indicator in the app. Typing a mode name in an ordinary web chat does not connect it.
  4. Manual editing pauses while connected, so provide requests and assets in the AI conversation. Disconnect to operate manually, and separately verify that external processing has stopped.
※ Tip

Simply typing a mode name in an ordinary web chat does not establish a connection.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Integration uses authenticated communication within your PC. Do not include connection details or authentication tokens in manuals, screenshots, public chats, or distribution ZIPs.

Requests such as Discuss Instructions Only or Test Without Connecting do not require starting integration or locking controls. Check the content and service terms before sending media to an external service.

Link to this explanation
Conversation with AI03Leave it to the AI, or discuss as you go?OpenClose

Even a simple request should state the purpose and required elements. Prefer an empty tab for new work.

  1. Specify what to make, landscape or portrait, text, assets, and how characters should be handled.
  2. For continued work, provide the project name and what to keep or change.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Even when overwriting the same tab, Start Over and Revise the Previous Project are different requests. Explicitly stating which one helps convey your intent.

Link to this explanation
Conversation with AI04Choose the destination and what may be remadeOpenClose

Specify not only the tab number but also whether the work is new or continued and which parts may be replaced.

  1. Verify the project name as well as the destination tab number. New work without a specified destination prefers an empty tab. Explicitly state the permitted replacement scope for an existing project.
  2. New work starts clean; continued work carries over approved assets and settings. Specify separately what to remake and what to preserve.
  3. For text, say whether you want to retype the content later or whether decorated text as an image is acceptable. Image-based lettering cannot be edited directly in the content field.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Dedicated Thumbnail requirements do not accept square orientation: specify landscape or portrait. Width/height must be 16–8192px, with no more than 32 million pixels total. Do not confuse this with the overall limits of normal Image editing.

For thumbnail characters, choose generated, supplied image, registered asset, or none. Also state whether supplied images may be modified. Changing generated text may require regeneration.

Link to this explanation
Conversation with AI05Try requesting a music video!OpenClose

Provide the song, lyrics, interval, orientation, and style. English songs and lyrics are supported too.

  1. For example: “Music-video mode. New project, empty tab. Portrait video, cute mood. Generate characters; you choose the details.”
  2. Provide the audio, lyrics, and section to use, then review the AI’s proposed theme.
  3. If you also need a finished MP4, include exporting in your request.
※ Tip

Align lyrics with the start of singing, not cut transitions.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

More generations or assets change the time and cost. Check the external AI provider's terms.

Link to this explanation
Conversation with AI06Try requesting a thumbnail!OpenClose

Explain the video or stream, the main wording, and the theme.

  1. For example: “Landscape. First-time horror-game playthrough. Use my supplied VTuber image and make ‘I want to go home…’ large.”
  2. Choose generated characters, a provided image, registered assets, or no character.
  3. Ask for people, backgrounds, and text on separate layers so they remain adjustable later.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Speech bubbles and generated logos are not required every time. Use them only when appropriate. Rasterized text differs from regular text that can be retyped.

Link to this explanation
Conversation with AI07Discuss comic structure and roughs firstOpenClose

Normally work one page at a time. Decide the story, characters, and art style, then review a rough that clearly shows the design.

  1. Decide genre, characters, setting, events, ending, and art style. Also state the planned page count and how far this 1 page should advance the story.
  2. Review panel layout, reading order, key moments, dialogue, and roughs showing faces, hair, and outfits clearly. Normally, approve these before final drawing.
  3. For subsequent pages, retain characters, outfits, left/right placement, locations, and actions from the previous page. Specify corrections by panel number and what to change or preserve.
  4. Dedicated automatic insertion is not currently available. Receive assets separated by role and confirm how to add them to the document through supported image import or manual placement.
! Caution

Dedicated automatic comic insertion is not implemented. Distinguish external asset creation from the document inside the app.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Distinguish written plans for the next page from artwork actually produced. Do not treat an unrequested next page as completed.

Preparing people, backgrounds, bubbles, text, and effects separately makes revisions easier. There is no feature that automatically reconstructs every original editable layer from one finished page image.

For continuation, carry forward approved designs, clothing, belongings, left/right consistency, time/place, and the previous page's action. Specify what changes and what stays.

Connected or advancing progress indicators alone do not confirm that a comic has been inserted or saved in the app.

Link to this explanation
Registered recipes and assets08Keep your own recipesOpenClose

Register a named method and reference assets, then specify them for your next creation.

  1. Summarize the mode, name, purpose, visual style or effects, and mandatory rules, then ask to register it. You can also create recipes adapted from existing types.
  2. Register generation references separately from assets to insert unchanged. These are app-managed copies independent of the original files.
  3. Specify the recipe name when using it. Each mode allows 30 entries; Recipe has a separate shared allowance of 30 across categories. Explicitly identify unwanted registrations before moving them to the Recycle Bin.
※ Tip

Each mode allows 30 entries. Recipe has a separate shared allowance of 30 across categories.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Each mode has a separate limit of 30 entries. Recipe has one shared 30-entry pool across Video, Image, and Comic, separate from the other modes' limits.

Coming Soon modes can also register instructions, but registration alone does not make production features available.

Currently, instruction changes are handled by registering under a new name or explicitly deleting an older version. Existing instructions are not automatically overwritten.

Link to this explanation
Registered recipes and assets09Rules for registered assets, names, and countsOpenClose

Separate reference assets from assets to insert unchanged, and save copies in the managed area.

  1. Specify purpose and registration name. Identical names count as duplicates.
  2. Register changed versions under new names, and explicitly identify only the unwanted older versions for deletion.
! Caution

Deleting a registration does not delete the original file or copies already placed in projects.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

MV, Thumbnail, Editing, Documents, and Comic each allow 30 entries. Recipe has a separate shared limit of 30 across Video, Image, and Comic. Old entries are not automatically deleted to make room at the limit.

The current dedicated operations do not support overwriting registered instruction text. Register under a new name, then explicitly delete an unwanted old version.

Even if a recipe registers multiple target domains, one integration locks only the specified Video, Image, or Comic workspace. Registration alone does not run cross-domain automatic insertion.

Link to this explanation
App integration screen10Workflow blocks and disconnectingOpenClose

Blocks show the work state reported by the AI. Recreating content can return a completed stage to In progress.

  1. The 7 blocks are stages reported by the AI, not percentages of elapsed time or estimates of time remaining. Multiple stages can progress at once.
  2. Recreating assets returns a stage from Complete to In progress. Insertion is the handoff to the app; verification checks the applied content and save state.
  3. If an error or interruption occurs, first check what has already been applied. Do not repeatedly insert the same content without checking.
  4. Use “Disconnect” to return to manual work. Applied edits remain; this does not roll back the project. Separately check that external AI processing or billing has stopped.
※ Tip

Disconnecting is not a rollback and does not necessarily stop external AI processing or charges.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Disconnect does not revert or delete the project. Nor does it necessarily stop external AI image generation, processing, or billing. Confirm cancellation on the external side too.

Integration expires if communication remains inactive. Initial requirement confirmation has a 2-hour deadline; subsequent updates normally renew a 20-minute deadline. This is not a guaranteed processing-time limit.

MV / Thumbnail completion occurs after the latest application and verification items have been checked. Closing the display alone does not confirm the project is saved.

Link to this explanation
App integration screen11Check how much is actually completeOpenClose

Asset creation, applying to the app, saving, and exporting a finished file are separate stages.

  1. For music videos, check lyrics, transitions, and audio. For thumbnails, check composition, text, and independent layers.
  2. Before making corrections, check the project name and destination tab.
※ Tip

A completed integration does not necessarily mean MP4 or PNG export is complete.

※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

Completed AI integration does not necessarily mean a final MP4, PNG, or other file has also been exported.

Before retrying an error, reconfirm the target and replacement scope so results are not applied to another tab or project without authorization.

Link to this explanation
App integration screen12When integration is not progressingOpenClose

Check the editing lock, communication, supported scope, and production requirements separately.

  1. If editing is locked, check the app’s integration state and the AI’s connection result. Do not assume a connection exists just because a mode name was given.
  2. Check the destination tab, new/continued work, required assets, and whether the mode is still in preparation. Asset creation and insertion into the app are separate stages.
  3. After an interruption, check what has been applied before resuming with a new connection. Use Disconnect to return to manual operation.
SymptomWhat to check
Another AI mode is connectedDisconnect the current integration before starting the desired mode.
Discussion works but nothing enters the appCheck whether the AI environment supports local connections and whether the mode supports automatic insertion. Comic, Recipe, Editing, and Documents have no dedicated insertion implementation.
The integration display is open but progress stopsCheck external AI processing and communication. Blocks are not an automatic timer; waiting alone does not advance them.
Registration failsCheck the 30-entry limit, duplicate names, instruction contents, and matching mode. Specify the target when deleting entries to make space.
Insertion failsCheck whether the source project changed, the destination tab, replacement permission, and supported files. First determine whether any content was partially applied.
Integration has endedExpired or disconnected sessions do not apply old requests. Reconfirm the target and start a new integration.
You want to edit manuallyUse Disconnect to regain control. Decide separately within the project whether to undo already applied contents.
※ NotesCheck usage distinctions and limitations＋

If the external AI continues working after disconnection, also give it stop or resume conditions in that conversation. Do not keep using the old session.

Link to this explanation
Multina13MV: Dopamine Rush

An opt-in style with beat-driven giant typography, neon, afterimages, split-and-merge effects and varied character motion.

  1. Ask the AI for “MV mode, Dopamine Rush” and discuss the audio, duration, assets, copy and destination.
  2. Start moving immediately and give each section a different featured effect. Keep rich lettering readable; do not copy the sample structure unchanged.
  3. Use the finished video and actual editor screenshot as references. The sample is not a preinstalled project.

No matching items

index.body:
前往说明
Multina使用说明书
精选功能推荐用法说明列表安装方法使用条款
主页

丰富功能等你发现！

Multina了解各项功能！

视频、图像、录屏，还有漫画。
从你想做的事情开始。

查看精选功能
找到感兴趣的内容
点击看看！
PICKUP

Multina精选功能！

一个工具，多种创作

4种创作功能，合而为一！

视频、图像、录屏、漫画。制作素材后，接着投入下一项创作。

  • 视频可编辑字幕、BGM和画面；图像可通过图层精细调整。
  • 从录屏走向视频制作；漫画与插画可使用画笔和分格绘制。
※ 补充

漫画与插画目前为试作版。

视频图像录制漫画·插画
